शकुनि: Śakuni m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 14, 13.
शकुल: Śakula m.: A kind of fish. Three of them, friends of one another, lived together in a shallow pond which abounded in fish; one of them was characteri-zed as Prāptakālajña ‘who knows the proper time (for action), who has the presence of mind’ (also called Saṃpratipattijña, Prati-pattimant, or Saṃpratipattimant 12. 135. 9, 13, 15), the other as Dīrghadarśin ‘who has forethought’, and the third as Dīrghasūtra ‘who procrastinates’; seeing, once, the water level falling down, Dīrghadarśin apprehended danger and told his friends that they had better quickly move out before their way to get out was cut off; Dīrghasūtra agreed with him but saw no reason to make haste; Saṃpratipattijña, however, said that he would not fail to take the correct course when time arrived; then Dīrghadarśin, of great intelligence, went out alone to a deep lake following a water current; when the water in the lake had thoroughly flown out the fisher-men began to catch the fish by various means; Dīrghasūtra got caught with others; when the fish that were caught were being tied to strings, Pratipattimant got himself mixed with those that were tied already and he held the string tight with his mouth (and thus escaped being actually tied by the string); when the fish, thus tied, were being washed in dirt-free water, Saṃprattimant gave up the string and escaped; the dull-witted and of low intelligence Dīrghasūtra, however, invited death on himself; thus one who does not recognize the most opportune time is destroyed like Dīrghasūtra; one like Saṃpra-tipattimant, who does not provide for his welfare in advance thinking himself to be clever, meets with danger; who, like Dīrgha-darśin, adopts proper course before the danger sets in, attains great bliss; this excellent आख्यान (आख्यानम् अनुत्तमम् 12. 135. 1) pertaining to the subject of deciding what should be done and what not was related by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira 12. 135. 1-19.
शक्रवापिन्: Śakravāpin m.: A serpent (पन्नग). Lived near the town Girivraja, in Magadha; described as ‘tormentor of enemies’ (शत्रुतापन) 2. 19. 9.
शङ्कुकर्ण: Śaṅkukarṇa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 14, 13.
शङ्ख: Śaṅkha m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 8; he was one of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12.
शङ्खनक: Śaṅkhanaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 11, 2.
शङ्खशिरस्: Śaṅkhaśiras m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 12, 2.
शङ्खशीर्ष: Śaṅkhaśīrṣa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
शबल: Śabala m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.
शरण: Śaraṇa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; some snakes of this family were dark-red, others white; all were ferocious, of huge shape and having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 6, 4.
शरभ: Śarabha m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Airāvata, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 10, 11.
शलकर: Śalakara m.: A mythical serpent 1. 52. 8 ? [See Śilin and Śilīśalakara]
शलपोतक: Śalapotaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.
शल्यक: Śalyaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 13, 2.
शशरोमन्: Śaśaroman m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the family of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 9, 7.
शार्दूली: Śārdūlī f.: A mythical female being. One of the nine self-born women (नारीः  … आत्मसंभवाः), daughters of Krodha-vaśā (or of Tāmrā (?) 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘given to anger, irascible’); she gave birth to lions, tigers and leopards 1. 60. 58-59, 63.
शालिपिण्ड: Śālipiṇḍa m.: A mythical serpent. Strong (वीर्यवान्) son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 14, 2.
शिखिन्: Śikhin m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
शितिकण्ठ: Śitikaṇṭha m.: A mythical serpent. One of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean; called अग्रतेजस् ‘having fierce lustre’; (or Agratejas a proper name ?) 16. 5. 15, 12. [See Agratejas]
शिरीषक: Śirīṣaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 14, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
शिलिन्: Śilin m.: A mythical serpent 1. 52. 8 ? [See Śilīśalakara]
शिलीशलकर: Śilīśalakara m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 8, 7, 9.
शुकी: Śukī f.: A mythical bird. One of the five famous daughters (लोक-विश्रुताः) of the divine (देवी) Tāmrā, she gave birth to parrots; described as ‘spirited’ (मनस्विनी), ‘endowed with auspicious qualities’ (कल्याणगुणसंपन्ना), and ‘adorned with all good marks’ (सर्वलक्षण-पूजिता) 1. 60. 54, 57.
शृङ्गवेग: Śṛṅgavega m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 11.
शेष: Śeṣa m.: A mythical serpent (नाग 1. 32. 24 (= Ananta); 1. 61. 91; 3. 194. 9, 10, 14; 5. 101. 2; भुजंगम 1. 32. 14), sometimes identified with Ananta; living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 1, 2. A. Birth and divine origin: Mentioned by Sūta as the first son of Kadrū, the second being Vāsuki (शेषः प्रथमतो जातो वासुकिस् तदनन्तरम् 1. 31. 5; hence called भुजगवराग्रज ‘elder brother of the excellent serpent’ (i. e. of Vāsuki) 1. 32. 22; listed as a काद्रवेय (son of Kadrū, daughter of Dakṣa) along with Ananta, Vāsuki and others 1. 59. 40; Bhīṣma told Duryodhana that Vāsudeva Janārdana created the divine Śeṣa who is known as Ananta 6. 63. 10. B. Epithets and Description: ad-orable (भगवन्त्) 1. 32. 2; lord (प्रभु) 1. 32. 5, (प्रभुर् भुवः) 1. 32. 22; to whom धर्म is god (धर्मदेव) 1. 32. 23; firm in truth (सत्यधृति) 1. 32. 6; of infinite coils (अनन्तभोग) 1. 32. 23; of boundless lustre (अमिततेजस्) 3. 194. 9; of great vigour (महौजस्) 6. 63. 11; excellent among serpents (पन्नगोत्तम) 1. 32. 16, (नागोत्तम) 1. 32. 23, (भुजंग-मोत्तम) 1. 32. 21, (पन्नगश्रेष्ठ) 7. 69. 48; described as ‘high as white mountain, wear-ing various ornaments, his tongues being like flames of fire, and of great strength’ (श्वेतो-च्चयनिभाकारो नानाविधविभूषणः । … ज्वालाजिह्वो महाबलः) 5. 101. 3; the big white snake issuing from the mouth of Bala-rāma is described as ‘having a thousand heads, having an expanse like that of a mountain, and having a red face’ (सहस्रशीर्षः पर्वता-भोगवर्ष्मा । रक्ताननः) where appare-ntly Śeṣa is meant, but is not directly named 16. 5. 12-13. C. Śeṣa's austerities and meeting with Brahmadeva: Śesa deserted his mother Kadrū and visited the slopes of the Himālayas; there on the Gandhamādana mountain and in Badarī, as also at other holy places like Gokarṇa, Puṣkarāraṇya and in various तीर्थस् and holy abodes (आयतनेषु 1. 32. 4) Śeṣa practised severe austerities living on wind and observing difficult vows; he lived all alone and had controlled his senses (एकान्तशीली, विजितेन्द्रियः 1. 32. 4); during the austerities he put on bark garments and wore matted hair; his flesh, skin and sinews dried up; when Pitāmaha Brahman, saw Śeṣa in this condition he asked him to do something beneficial to the people instead of tormenting them by his severe austerities; he asked Śeṣa the reason for undertaking the austerities; Śeṣa told Pitāmaha that his serpent brothers were dull-witted; they envied each other and did not suffer either Vinatā or her son (Vainateya Garuḍa) who was their cousin; they hated Garuḍa; Śeṣa there-fore did not want to see his brothers nor live with them; Śeṣa undertook austerities to give up his body and to avoid the company of his brothers in the next life; he asked Pitāmaha's permission to do that 1. 32. 5-12; Brahman told Śeṣa that his brothers faced danger because they had offended their mother but that incident had been taken care of; since Śeṣa was devoted to righteousness (दिष्ट्या च बुद्धिर् धर्मे ते 1. 32. 16), Pitāmaha offered him a boon 1. 32. 13-16; Śeṣa desired to find pleasure in righteousness (धर्म), equanimity (शम), and austerity (तपस्) 1. 32. 17. D. Śeṣa as supporter of the earth: Brahman was pleased with Śeṣa's self-control and equanimity and asked him to collect the earth properly and hold it so that it became steady for the benefit of the creatures; Śeṣa agreed to do what Brahman desired and asked Brahman to place the earth on his head; Brahman asked him to go below the earth for which earth would provide an opening (विवर) 1. 32. 21-22; Śeṣa entered the earth through a cleft and held the divine (देवी) earth, girdled by the oceans, after enclosing it on all sides; he made the earth firm 1. 32. 19-22; 5. 101. 2; 6. 63. 10; 7. 69. 48; for this feat of holding the earth Śeṣa compared with Brahman or with Balabhid (Indra) 1. 32. 23; (here called नाग Ananta) dwells all alone below the earth 1. 32. 24; Brahman gave to Śeṣa Vaina-teya Suparṇa (i. e. Garuḍa) as his friend 1. 32. 25. E. Association with Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa: Nārāyaṇa told Mārkaṇḍeya that he, having become Śeṣa, supports the earth surrounded by the four oceans and adorned by Meru and Mandara 3. 187. 10; when the entire creation, both moving and non-moving, gets lost in one single ocean, god Viṣṇu Nārā-yaṇa sleeps alone on the bed of water on the huge body of Śeṣa; at that time with Śeṣa's great coil Viṣṇu encompasses the whole earth and sustains it 3. 194. 8-10; Hari Nārāyaṇa when he is in his निद्रायोग also sleeps on the bed in the form of the body of the snake (Śeṣa not named here) which is arranged on water 12. 335. 57-58, 17. F. Śeṣa's place in the four व्यूहस् of the Pāñcarātra system: Nārāyaṇa told Nārada that his fourth form (मूर्ति) created imperishable (अव्यय) Śeṣa who is known as Saṃka-rṣaṇa; from him was created Pradyumna 12. 326. 68; जीव is called Śeṣa Saṃkarṣaṇa 12. 326. 35. G. Other features of his eminence: (1) A जीव, before attaining सिद्धि (12. 271. 44) passes through various courses before he reaches the undecaying and infinite place of Viṣṇu, Brahman, Śeṣa, and Nara 12. 271. 50; (2) Droṇa while blessing Duryodhana says: “May Śeṣa, the eminent among the serpents, grant well being (स्वस्ति) to you” 7. 69. 48; (3) Baladeva was the incarnation of a portion of Śeṣa 1. 61. 91; (4) He with other snakes came to greet Arjuna's birth 1. 114. 60.
श्येनी: Śyenī1 f.: A mythical female bird. One of the five famous (लोकविश्रुताः) daughters of the divine (देवी) Tāmrā, she gave birth to falcons 1. 60. 54, 55; [identical with Śyenī2 ?]
Śyenī2 f.: A mythical female bird. Wife of Aruṇa, she gave birth to two heroic and strong sons—Saṃpāti and Jaṭāyus 1. 60. 67; [identical with Śyenī1 ?]
श्रीवह: Śrīvaha m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 13, 2.
श्रुतसेन: Śrutasena m.: A mythical serpent. Referred to by Uttaṅka in his praise of the Nāgas as follows: “The youngest brother (जघन्यज) of Takṣaka, known as Śruta-sena; aspiring to be the chief of the Nāgas he lived in Mahaddyuman; I would like to do obeissance to him at all times.” 1. 3. 146.
श्वसन: Śvasana m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the family of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he was one of those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 13.
श्वेत: Śveta m.: Name of one of the cardinal elephants (दिशागज). Son of Śvetā, who was one of the dau-ghters of Krodhavaśā (or of Tāmrā ? 1. 60. 54); quick in his gait (आशुग) 1. 60. 64.
Śveta, Śvetagraha m.: Designation of the planet Ketu. [See Ketu in the Addenda]

Śveta m.: Name of a mountain. A. Origin: The seed secreted by Rudra became the Śveta mountāin (रुद्रेण शुक्रम् उत्सृष्टं तच् छ्वेतः पर्वतो ऽभवत्) 3. 218. 27. B. Location: In the north (उदीच्याम्) 7. 57. 23; in the north, beyond the Himavant and Niṣkuṭa mountains 2. 24. 27; beyond the Śveta is the land of the Kiṃ-puruṣas (श्वेतपर्वतं … समतिक्रम्य … देशं किंपुरुषावासम्) 2. 25. 1; in the vicinity of the Uṣīrabīja, Malnāka and Kāla-śaila mountains 3. 140. 1, and of Mandara 3. 140. 4; the Ramaṇaka varṣa is to the south of Śveta and to the north of Nīla 6. 9. 2; to the south of Śṛṅgin and to the north of Śveta is the Hairaṇvata varṣa 6. 9. 5; one of the six mountains listed by Saṃjaya which extend to the east (प्रागायताः) and merge at both ends in the eastern and the western ocean (अवगाढा ह्य् उभयतः समुद्रौ पूर्व-पश्चिमौ) 6. 7. 2; the distance between these mountains is thousands of योजनस् (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो योजनानि सहस्रशः) 6. 7. 4. C. Description: Shining (शुभ) 3. 155. 28; big mountain (महागिरि) 3. 214. 30; 9. 59. 8; huge (अतिप्रमाण) 5. 47. 66; king of mountains (पर्वतराजन्) 3. 155. 4; excellent among mountains (शिखरिणां वरम्) 3. 155. 4; heap of rocks (शिलोच्चय) 5. 47. 66; having many summits (नाना-समुच्छ्रय) 3. 155. 28; its top (शैल-पृष्ठ) not easy to reach (सुदुर्गम) 3. 214. 12; having bright forests (शुभकानन) 3. 220. 22; covered with thickets of reeds (शरस्तम्बैः सुसंवृतम्) 3. 214. 10; golden (काञ्चन) 3. 220. 21; delightful due to gold and jewels (मङीकाञ्चनरम्य) 3. 155. 28; inlaid with silver (रजताचित) 3. 186. 102; 13. 151. 26, and bright like silver (रजतप्रभ) 6. 7. 3 (does रजत here stand for महारजत ‘gold’ ?); variegated due to many kinds of minerals (बहुधातुविचित्र) 9. 59. 8; looking like a big dense cloud (महा-भ्रघनसंकाशं), and full of water (सलिलोपहितम्) 3. 155. 28; full of Rakṣases, Piśācas, frightful Bhūtas, Rākṣasīs, and many animals and birds (रक्षोभिश् च पिशाचैश् च रौद्रैर् भूतगणैस् तथा । राक्षसी-भिश् च सम्पूर्णम् अनेकैश् च मृगद्वि-जैः) 3. 214. 11; all the six mountains listed by Saṃjaya are described as stretching to-wards the east (प्रागायताः), jewelled moun-tains (रत्नपर्वताः), and frequented by the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारण-सेविताः) 6. 7. 2, 4 (also see the next section). D. Characteristics: (1) On the Śvetagiri (and Mandara) live the Yakṣa Māṇicara and Kubera, the king of the Yakṣas; eighty-eight thousand quick moving (शीघ्रचारिणः) Gandharvas, Kiṃpuruṣas and their four times Yakṣas, having many forms and weapons serve there Māṇibhadra, the chief of the Yakṣas 3. 140. 4-6; (2) The mountain is protected by strange snakes having seven heads and poisonous eyes (दृष्टिविषैः सप्त-शीर्षैर् गुप्तं भोगिभिर् अद्भुतैः) 3. 214. 11; (3) Śveta mountain shone with the flowering Saṃtānaka forests, forests of Kara-vīra, Pārijāta, Japā and Aśoka trees, clusters of Kadamba trees and hosts of heavenly animals and birds (दिव्यैर् मृगगणैर् अपि । दिव्यैः पक्षिगणैश् चैव शुशुभे श्वेत-पर्वतः) 3. 220. 23-24; (4) Are the Śveta and the other mountains listed by Brahman to be looked upon as characterized by the middle quality (मध्यम गुण), i. e. by the quality रजस् ? 14. 43. 4, 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः). E. Importance: (1) Listed by Brahman among mountains called ‘kings of mountains’ (पर्वतराजा-नः) 14. 43. 4; (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2. F. Epic events: (1) Arjuna, in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya, reached the Śveta mountain after conquering the peoples on the Himavant and the Niṣkūṭa mountains and lived there 2. 24. 2; he then crossed Śveta and conquered the country of the Kiṃpuruṣas 2. 25. 1-2; (2) The Pāṇḍavas in their journey northwards in the company of Lomaśa were to enter it and proceed to inaccessible mountains 3. 140. 1, 4, 8; it was agreed that the Pāṇḍa-vas were to meet Arjuna, who had left for heavenly missiles, on the Śveta mountain at the end of the fifth year of Arjuna's student-ship 3. 155. 3-5; after killing Jaṭāsura, the Pāṇḍavas entered Śveta from Nārāyaṇā-śrama (3. 155. 1) on the fourth day (पर्-वतं विविशुः श्वेतं चतुर्थे ऽहनि पाण्ड-वाः) 3. 155. 27; (3) Seen by Arjuna during the night on his way to the north to propitiate Śiva for his Pāśupata 7. 57. 23. G. Past and mythological events: (1) When Nahuṣa became the king of heaven he enjoyed at many places, one of them being the Śveta mountain 5. 11. 9; (2) The sage Mārkaṇḍeya saw Śveta among other moun-tains in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 102; (3) When Dakṣa's daughter Svāhā in the form of Śivā, the wife of Aṅgiras, held the seed of Agni she took the form of a Suparṇī Garuḍī and flew away; when she saw Śveta she poured the seed in a golden pot on the top of the mountain; this she did six times on each प्रतिपद् day; Kumāra (Skanda) with six heads was born; the child played on the top of the mountain 3. 213. 52; 3. 214. 1, 7, 9-10, 15, 17, 26; the Kṛttikās gathered (?) the seed of Pāvaka (Agni) on the mountain Śveta (पावकस्येन्द्रियं श्वेते कृत्तिकाभिः कृतं नगे) 3. 218. 27; the child Kumāra sitting on the top of the mountain saw all directions by his different heads; he drew his bow and shot arrows at Śveta and pierced the Krauñca mountain, the son of Himavant; he then hurled a शक्ति which by its impact broke the summit of Śveta; the mountain, afraid, deserted the earth and flew up in the sky with other mountains; later Śveta return-ed to the earth 3. 214. 27, 30-31, 34-35, 37; Skanda, surrounded by hosts of Piśācas and gods, shone on the golden mountain Śveta; the whole world, including Indra, looked at the delighted Skanda and was not tired of looking at him; there were also the rest of gods and all great sages to look at Skanda; there one heard the sounds of musical instruments, of the dancing heavenly Gandharvas and Apsarases and of the delighted beings 3. 220. 21, 25-27; (4) Rāmāyaṇa events: (i) Avindhya, an old learned Rākṣasa, saw in a dream that while Kumbhakarṇa and other demons, wearing red garlands, were being dragged to the south, Vibhīṣaṇa and his four counsellors alone, with white parasole and head-gear, all wearing white garlands, mounted on top of the Śveta mountain 3. 264. 65-67; (ii) a Guhyaka, with marvellous water sent by Kubera, arrived from Śveta mountain to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa 3. 273. 9. H. Use in an illustration: According to Arjuna one who wants to win victory in a battle over Vāsu-deva wants to split the huge Śveta mountain with his palm; in such an effort his palm, along with nails, will be shattered and he will do no harm to the mountain (गिरिं य इच्छेत तलेन भेत्तुं शिलोच्चयं श्वेतम् अतिप्रमाणम् । तस्यैव पाणिः सनखो विशीर्येन् न चापि किंचित् स गिरेस् तु कुर्यात्) 5. 47. 66.

C. Characteristics: They are devoted to god Puruṣottama (ते भक्ताः पुरुषोत्तमम्) 12. 323. 24; (भक्ताश् च पुरुषोत्तमम्) 12. 331. 41; (नारायणपर) 12. 323. 24; (मद्भक्ताः) 12. 326. 18; they lick the god with devotion (i. e. they are absorbed in devotion (? लेलिह्यन्ते … भक्त्या देवम्) 12. 322. 11-12 (Nī. on 12. 335. 11: जीह्वाभिर् इव स्वाङ्गभूताभी रसनाशक्तिभिर् लेलिह्यन्ते पायसम् इव लिहन्ति); they are absorbed in complete devotion (एकान्तभावोपगत) 12. 323. 24; they are devoted to one god (एकान्तिन्) 12. 323. 26, 42 (Nī. on 12. 348. 3: एकान्-तिनो निष्कामभक्ताः); 12. 326. 19; (एक-भावम् अनुव्रताः) 12. 323. 45; (एकाग्राश् चिन्तयेयुर् माम्) 12. 326. 18; completely engrossed in ब्रह्मन् (ब्रह्मभावम् अनुष्ठिताः) 12. 323. 45; they always wor-ship the (one) god and he sports with them (ते ऽर्चयन्ति सदा देवं तैः सार्धं रमते च सः) 12. 331. 42; they are en-lightened (प्रतिबुद्ध) 12. 331. 41; their mode of devotion (जप) and offering बलि as well as the result of their devotion and offering described in 12. 323. 32, 36-41; Nārada thought that Nara and Nārāyaṇa (their description in 12. 331. 23-27) were like the men he saw in the Śvetadvīpa 12. 331. 30; they are so blessed that if one saw the people on the Śvetadvīpa it was as good as seeing the god himself (दृष्टो भवति देवेश एभिर् दृष्टैर् … ) 12. 323. 47; the people of Śvetadvīpa had the same characteristic as that of the liberated men (ये विमुक्ता भवन्तीह  … तेषां लक्षणम् एतद् धि यच् छ्वेत-द्वीपवासिनाम्) 12. 322. 14 (Nī. on 12. 335. 14; श्वेतद्वीपवासिनां जीवन्मुक्तानां च निरिन्द्रियत्वादिकं एव लक्षणम्); (at the end of their life) they enter the eternal god of thousand lustres (ते सह-स्रार्चीषं देवं प्रविशन्ति सनातनम्) 12. 323. 25; (मां प्रवेक्ष्यन्त्य् असं-शयम्) 12. 326. 19. D. Epic events: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Bhīṣma how the people of the Śvetadvīpa were born and what was the kind of life they were going to obtain after death (कथं ते पुरुषा जाताः का तेषां गतिर् उत्तमा) 12. 322. 13; thereupon Bhīṣma replied to his question in details starting with the story of king Uparicara 12. 322. 16 ff.; Bhīṣma also told Yudhiṣṭhira how Nārada went to Śvetadvīpa 12. 324. 39; (2) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana why Nārada return-ed from the Śvetadvīpa to the Badarī आश्रम to see Nara and Nārāyaṇa, how long he stayed there, and what were the questions he asked to those two Ṛṣis 12. 331. 15-18; thereupon Vaiśaṃpāyana re-plied to his question in details 12. 331. 19 ff. E. Past events: (1) Nārada standing on a peak of mountain Meru saw the Śveta-dvīpa in the north-west direction as a wonderful spectacle 12. 322. 7-8; Nārada reached the Śvetadvīpa and saw the people there; he respected them by bowing down and they honoured him mentally (पूजयाम् आस शिरसा मनसा तैश् च पूजि-तः) 12. 325. 1-2; Bhagavān appeared before Nārada, but told him to leave the island immediately so that no disturbance was caused to the contemplations of the people of the Śvetadvīpa (गच्छ नारद माचिरम् ॥ … एकाग्राश् चिन्तयेयुर् मां नैषां विघ्नो भवेद् इति) 12. 326. 17-18; 12. 331. 13; he left Śvetadvīpa and went to mount Meru and from there to Gandha-mādana to reach Badarī 12. 331. 20-22; (also see the two epic events above); Nārada told Nara and Nārāyaṇa that he saw in Śvetadvīpa the people residing there 12. 331. 29-30; Nārāyaṇa asked Nārada if he saw in Śvetadvīpa the Bhagavān who was their (i. e. of Nara and Nārāyaṇa) higher प्रकृति (अपि … स भगवान् … श्वेतद्वीपे त्वया दृष्ट आवयोः प्रकृतिः परा) 12. 331. 35; Nārada replied that he did and also told them he saw the white people who were devoid of all sense-organs; as directed by Bhagavān he returned from Śvetadvīpa 12. 331. 36, 41, 51; 12. 332. 1; Nara and Nārāyaṇa then told Nārada that they too had seen him (Nārada) meeting the Bhaga-vān himself in Śvetadvīpa and had heard his conversation with him (आवाभ्याम् अपि दृष्टस् त्वं श्वेतद्वीपे … । समागतो भग-वता संजल्पं कृतवान् यथा ॥ ) 12. 332. 22; (2) A noncorporeal voice told Ekata, Dvita and Trita, who were practising severe austerities on mountain Meru to go to Śvetadvīpa where the Bhagavān had mani-fested himself (गच्छध्वं तत्र) (i. e. Śvetadvīpa) मुनयस् तत्रात्मा मे प्र-काशितः) 12. 323. 21-23, 26; they reached the Śvetadvīpa by following the way told to them by the noncorporeal voice; having reached the island, however, their eyes were blinded and they could not see any man (प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं … ततो नो दृष्टिविषयस् तदा प्रतिहतो ऽभवत्) 12. 323. 27-28; when Ekata, Dvita and Trita further practised austerities for a hundred years they were able to see the people of the Śveta island; they had folded their hands and, facing north-east, they did the जप of Brahman; that जप was mental (नित्याञ्जलिकृतान् ब्रह्म जपतः प्रागुदङ्-मुखान् । मानसो नाम स जपो जप्यते तैर् महात्मभिः ॥ ) 12. 323. 32; suddenly they saw lustre equal to that of a thousand suns; the people of the island together be-gan to run quickly, folding their hands and, delighted, they continued to say ‘नमस्’; when they were thus showing their reve-rence, we heard a loud sound (ततो ऽभि-वदतां तेषाम् अश्रौष्म विपुलं ध्वनिम्) 12. 323. 37; Ekata, Dvita and Trita were not able to see anything, but they could hear the praise of Bhagavān; at that time wind blew heavenly flowers and plants suitable for offerings; with that, people gave offering to Hari (बलिः किलोपह्रियते तस्य देवस्य तैर् नरैः); indeed, the god himself had arrived there when they were uttering sounds; from among those thou-sands of men no one welcomed them mentally, nor by looking at them; no one thought of them and hence they were worried (एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे वायुः … दिव्यान्य् उवाह पुष्पाणि कर्मण्याश् चौषधिस् तथा ॥  … चिन्ताव्याकुलितात्मानो जाताः स्मो … । मानवानां सहस्रेषु तेषु … । अस्मान् न कश्चिन् मनसा चक्षुषा वाप्य् अपूजयत् ॥ … नास्मासु दधिरे भावम्) 12. 323. 38-45; a non-corporeal being then told them that they had already seen the white people of the island and that seeing them was as good as seeing the chief god; they should therefore quit the island without delay (उवाच खस्थं किम् अपि भूतं तत्रा-शरीरकम् ॥ दृष्टा वः पुरुषाः श्वेताः … दृष्टो भवति देवेश एभिर् दृष्टैर् द्विजोत्त-माः ॥ ) 12. 323. 46-47; Bhagavān told Nārada that Ekata, Dvita and Trita had come to the Śveta island desirous of his दर्शन, but they could not see him (इमं देशम् अनुप्राप्ता मम दर्शनलालसाः) 12. 326. 11; (3) Vaiśaṃpāyana informed Janamejaya that Nārada had told the Sātvata धर्म to Vyāsa, which was, also called the धर्म of the Ekāntins, followed by the white ascetics (धर्मः सात्वतो … । एवं हि … नारदो गुरवे मम । श्वेतानां यतीनाम् आह एकान्तगतिम् अव्ययाम् ॥ ) 12. 336. 76, 78-79 (These ‘white ascetics’ are probably to be identified with the people of the Śvetadvīpa. Nī., however, on 12. 348. 85; श्वेतानां गृहस्थादीनाम् । यतीनां काषायधारिणाम्).
श्वेता: Śvetā f.: A mythical female elephant (?) One of the nine daughters of Krodha-vaśā (or of Tāmrā ? 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘irascible’), she gave birth to the cardinal elephant Śveta 1. 60. 59, 64.
शकटव्यूह: Śakaṭavyūha m.: Name of a व्यूह (a particular arrangement of the army) 7. 6. 15. Droṇa arranged the Kaurava army in the form of the Śakaṭavyūha on the eleventh day of the war; Jayadratha, the Kaliṅga king (not named), and Vikarṇa stood on the right side (दक्षिण पार्श्व); at the extremity of the right wing (प्रपक्ष) was Śakuni, assisted by excellent horsemen from the Gandhāra country who fought with sharp प्रासस्; Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman, Citrasena, and Viviṃśati, with Duḥśāsana to lead them (दुःशासनमुखाः), stood on its left side (सव्य पार्श्व); at the extremity of the left wing (प्रपक्ष) stood the Kāmbojas, led by Sudakṣiṇa, who fought on horses, as also the Śakas and the Yavanas; apparently in between the two sides were stationed the Madras, the Trigartas, the Ambaṣṭhas, warriors who came from the west and the north, the Śibis, the Śūrasenas, the Śūdras, the Maladas, the Sauvīras, and the Kitavas, all of whom were led by Duryo-dhana (तवात्मजं पुरस्कृत्य); Karṇa took position in front of Duryodhana and was at the head of all the archers (प्रमुखे सर्वधन्विनाम्) 7. 6. 1-8; in this Vyūha, Karṇa was in front of the army (तावकानां मुखं कर्णः) 7. 6. 21; from the description of the start of that day's battle it is clear that Droṇa also stood at the head of the army 7. 6. 32-36; this Vyūha of the Kauravas was opposed by the Pāṇḍavas with the Krauñcavyūha 7. 6. 15. [See Cakraśakaṭa]
शक्ति: Śakti1 f.: A missile special to Vāsava (Indra), hence called वासवी 3. 294. 34; 7. 122. 33; 7. 148. 34; 7. 158. 9, 10, 56, 58; given by Vāsava 3. 286. 20; 7. 154. 50; 7. 155. 21; or by Śakra (Indra) 3. 294. 1ff.; 7. 154. 53, 58 (शक्रशक्ति); 7. 155. 27; 1. 7. 156. 27; 7. 157. 4. A. Description: unfailing (अमोघा) 3. 286. 14; 3. 294. 20, 21, 24, 29, 33; 7. 157. 7, 12, 16, 29; heavenly (दिव्या) 8. 5. 65; best, excellent (श्रेष्ठा) 7. 154. 52; (उत्तमा) 7. 154. 55; (परमा) 7. 157. 6; (प्रवरा) 3. 294. 29; honoured (सत्कृता) 7. 154. 53; (पूज्यमाना) 7. 122. 33; irresisti-ble (अनिवार्या) 7. 158. 2; unbearable (असह्या) 7. 154. 52; 7. 158. 2; burning, shining (like a lightning) (प्रज्वलन्ती) 7. 122. 33; (ज्व-लन्ती) 7. 154. 57; (प्रज्वलिता) 3. 294. 35; (प्रदीप्ता) 7. 154. 54; दीप्यमाना 7. 148. 34; 7. 154. 57; (विद्युत्प्रभा) 8. 5. 65; deco-rated with gold (कनकभूषणा) 8. 5. 65; victorious (वैजयन्ती) 7. 154. 52; the highway to victory (जयस्य च परायणम्) 7. 157. 6; killer of one opponent (when used by Karṇa) (एकघ्नी) 7. 158. 2; destroyer of the body of the enemy (परकायापहन्त्री) 7. 154. 55; killer of many enemies (when used by Indra) (द्विषतां हन्त्री) 8. 5. 65; (अमित्रविनिबर्हिणी) 3. 286. 14; (शत्रुसङ्घानां घातिनीम्) 3. 294. 21; having a terrible form (रौद्ररूपं बिभर्ति च) 7. 148. 34. B. Exchanged by Indra for Karṇa's armour and ear-rings: God Sūrya advised Karṇa to obtain from Indra his unfailing Śakti in exchange for (नियमेन) the armour (कवच) and the ear-rings (कुण्डलस्) which Indra would ask Karṇa to part with 3. 286. 14-15; after receiving this hint, Karṇa long-ing for the Śakti waited for Vāsava (Indra) 3. 286. 20; when Indra came and begged Karṇa of his कवच and कुण्डलस्, Karṇa asked Indra's unfailing Śakti in return 3. 294. 20-21; Indra agreed to part with his Śakti under the stipulation that although the Śakti, when used by Indra, would unfailingly kill Indra's enemies ब्य् हुन्द्रेद्स् and return to Indra's (user's) hand, when it reached Karṇa it would kill only ओने illustrious, roaring and tormenting enemy of Karṇa and return, not to Karṇa, but to Indra (सेयं तव करं प्रा-प्य हत्वैकं रिपुम् ऊर्जितम् । गर्जन्तं प्रतपन्तं च माम् एवैष्यति सूतज ॥ ) 3. 294. 23-25; the Śakti, as long as it was with Karṇa, would fail after killing one hero and would lose its quality of being unfailing (एकवीरवधे मोघा) 7. 157. 1, 7; (अमो-घाया विघातार्थम्) 7. 157. 12; Karṇa agreed to receive the Śakti on that condition for he feared danger in battle only from one enemy 3. 294. 26, 29; Indra also warned Karṇa not to use the Śakti when other missiles were available with him and when he was not in danger; if used negligently the Śakti would boomerang on Karṇa (विद्य-मानेषु शस्त्रेषु यद्य् अमोघाम् असंशये । प्रमत्तो मोक्ष्यसे चापि त्वय्येवैषा पतिष्यति ॥ ) 3. 294. 33; Karṇa vowed to Indra (सत्यम् एतद् ब्रवीमि ते) that he would release the Vāsavī (Śakti) only when he was in great danger 3. 294. 34; Karṇa then received the burning Sakti in exchange of his कवच and कुण्डलस् 3. 294. 35, 38; 8. 5. 65. C. What the Śakti meant to Karṇa: Karṇa had great confidence due to the Śakti (अयं च प्रत्ययः कर्णे शक्त्या) 7. 157. 31; when Vāsava (Indra) gave the Śakti to Karṇa, he (Karṇa) felt that Arjuna was as good as dead 7. 155. 21-22; with Śakti in Karṇa's hand, no one in the world dare oppose him 7. 155. 13; Karṇa had preserved the Śakti to kill Arjuna 7. 122. 33; 7. 148. 34; 7. 154. 53; the Śakti meant death for Arjuna 7. 157. 38; Duḥśāsana, Śakuni, Jayadratha and Duryodhana always counselled Karṇa not to use the Śakti against any one except Arjuna 7. 157. 32-34; (cf. 7. 157. 19-21 for the use of Śakti (not named) only against Arjuna or Kṛṣṇa); if on any occasion Karṇa's other missiles had failed and if he was pressed (पीडितः) by the circums-tances, he would certainly have used his Vāsavī Śakti against Arjuna 7. 158. 54; hence Kṛṣṇa protected Arjuna particularly from the unfailing Śakti which, if released, would certainly have killed him like the light-ning striking down a tree 7. 157. 16; according to Vyāsa too if Arjuna and Karṇa had clashed, the latter, after exhaus-ting all other missiles, would have surely used Vāsavī against Arjuna 7. 158. 56; Kṛṣṇa was therefore always looking for a way to render the unfailing Śakti futile (अमोघां तां कथं शक्तिं मोघां कुर्याम्) 7. 157. 29; when the Śakti was diverted on Ghaṭotkaca, Karṇa, in the opinion of Kṛṣṇa, was as good as dead 7. 155. 12; when Karṇa was relieved of his Śakti, he became an ordinary human being (सो ऽद्य मानुषतां प्राप्तो विमुक्तः शक्रदत्तया 7. 155. 27), and Arjuna could dare attack him 8. 22. 33. D. Why the Śakti was not used against Arjuna: Both Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Sātyaki asked Saṃjaya and Kṛṣṇa respectively why the Śakti was not used by Karṇa against Arjuna 7. 157. 1; 7. 158. 2-3; 7. 157. 31; (1) accor-ding to Saṃjaya's reporting, Duryodhana, Śakuni, Duḥśāsana, and he himself urged Karṇa every night after the day's war to use his Śakti the next day against Arjuna or Kṛṣṇa (7. 157. 19-21), but that counsel was forgotten the next day during the fight due to the watchfulness of Kṛṣṇa (सा तु बुद्धिः कृताप्य् एवं जाग्रति त्रिदशेश्वरे । अप्रमेये हृषीकेशे युद्धकाले व्यमुह्यत) 7. 157. 27; Kṛṣṇa also never brought Arjuna face to face with Karṇa as long as the latter was equipped with Śakti; Kṛṣṇa managed to see that other warriors faced Karṇa 7. 157. 28-29; according to Saṃjaya, again, the previous night's counsel (7. 158. 4-5) was forgotten by Karṇa the next day due to the deities (unfavorable) to him and to the other heroes (on the side of the Kauravas), and thus it was primarily due to the working of the fate that Karṇa did not employ his Śakti against Arjuna or Kṛṣṇa to kill any one of them (ततः प्रभातसमये राजन् कर्णस्य दैवतैः । अन्येषां चैव योधानां सा बुद्धिर् नश्यते पुनः ॥ दैवम् एव परं मन्ये यत् कर्णो हस्तसंस्थया । न जघान रणे पार्थं कृष्णं वा देवकी-सुतम् ॥ 7. 158. 6-7; also 8-9; (2) accor-ding to Vyāsa too it was due to fate (दिष्ट्या) that Arjuna was not locked in a duel with Karṇa prior to the latter's being relieved of the Śakti 7. 158. 54; according to him Ghaṭotkaca was killed by Time using Vāsavī as his means (वासवीं कारणं कृत्वा कालेनापहतो ह्य् असौ) 7. 158. 58; (3) according to Kṛṣṇa he deluded the mind of Karṇa and hence he did not use his Śakti against Arjuna (अहम् एव तु राधेयं मोहयामि युधां वर 7. 157. 37; (4) according to Dhṛtarāṣṭra both fate and the intelligence of Kṛṣṇa came together to defeat the purpose of the Kauravas and hence the Vāsavī (Śakti) killed Ghaṭotkaca instead of Arjuna (दैवेनैव हता यूयं स्वबुद्ध्या केशवस्य च । गता हि वासवी हत्वा तृणभूतं घटोत्कचम्) 7. 158. 10. E. Use: (1) By Karṇa: All the Kuru warriors urged Karṇa to kill the demon Ghaṭotkaca by using the Śakti given to him by Vāsava and save the Kauravas and their warriors from destruction; hearing that call, Karṇa held the Śakti desiring to kill Ghaṭot-kaca, that Śakti given to him by Śakra and which he had preserved for Arjuna for years; when the missile was released, Ghaṭotkaca, afraid, assumed a huge form of the foot of the Vindhya mountain and fled; the beings in the mid-region wailed at the sight of the Śakti; the released Śakti first burnt the माया of Ghaṭotkaca, and then broke open deeply the chest of Ghaṭot-kaca and went up in the sky, shining at night, to enter the spaces between the नक्षत्रस् (ऊर्ध्वं ययौ दीप्यमाना निशायां नक्षत्राणाम् अन्तराण्य् आविशन्ती 7. 154. 57); Ghaṭotkaca, with his vitals pierced by the Śakti, was killed 7. 154. 48-59; 7. 156. 24; 7. 158. 10; 8. 5. 71; by asking Ghaṭotkaca to fight with Karṇa, Kṛṣṇa diverted the Śakti on him 7. 156. 27; 7. 157. (5), 6, 39; 7. 155. 12, 14; (Kṛṣṇa said that if Karṇa had not killed Ghaṭotkaca with his Śakti, he would have killed Ghaṭotkaca 7. 156. 25); (2) By Indra: When used by Indra while fighting with the Daityas, the Śakti, after killing his enemies by hun-dreds, returned to Indra's hand 3. 294. 24; 3. 286. 16 (killing of the enemies by hundreds and thousands). [See Śakti2-5]

Śakti2 f., Śaktyastra nt.: missile of Skanda. Described as terrific (भीमम् nt.) 9. 45. 60, (सुघोरा f.) 9. 45. 62; its association with Skanda noticed when it is described that in the entourage of Śiva, Skanda, on his peacock, stood on the side of Devī, holding Śakti on his neck (शक्तिम् कण्ठे समादाय) 13. 14. 143; it was used by Skanda against the demon Tāraka and his associates; Skanda released it again and again, imbibing it with his own lustre (आदधच् चात्मनो तेजः 9. 45. 60); when released, the flame of the meteor and resounding thunder-bolts struck the earth as would happen at the time of the end of the world; when one Śakti was hurled by Skanda, crores of Śaktis fell out from it; Skanda killed with his missile the demons Tāraka, Mahiṣa, Tripāda and Hradodara together with innumerable Daityas; they were burnt by the flames of the Śaktyastra 9. 45. 60-70. [See Śakti1, 3-5]
Śakti3 f.: Missile, special to Viśākha. When Viśākha came out of the right side of Skanda's body he appeared armed with Śakti (शक्तिधृक्) 3. 216. 13. [See Śakti1-2, 4-5]

Śakti4 f.: Missile of Kṛṣṇa. Along with other missiles and weapons (प्रहरणानि), Śakti appeared on one of the arms of Kṛṣṇa when he manifested his fierce form in the Sabhā of the Kauravas 5. 129. 9-10; Kṛṣṇa asked his charioteer Dāruka to place in his chariot the divine (दिव्या) Śakti when the chariot was to be made ready for Kṛṣṇa's eventual intervention in the war 7. 56. 32 [See Śakti1-3, 5]
Śakti5 f.: Missile of Aṃśa. When Indra got ready to fight with Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the time of burning the Khāṇḍava forest, Aṃśa, to help Indra, picked up his Śakti 1. 218. 33. [See Śakti1-4]
शतघण्टा: Śataghaṇṭā1 f.: Name of the गदा of Ghaṭotkaca (or adj. of his गदा, meaning ‘decorated with a hundred bells’ ?). Described as bright like burning fire, decorated, adorned with gold ornaments and making loud noise (दीप्ताग्निसंकाशा, अलंकृता, काञ्चनभूषणा, महास्वना); Ghāṭotkaca, when struck on his head by Alāyudha with a huge परिघ, hurled at his opponent his Śataghaṇṭā गदा which crushed Alāyudha's horses, chariot, and the charioteer 7. 153. 13-14. [See Śataghaṇṭā2]

Śataghaṇṭā2 f.: Name of the गदा of Vibhīṣaṇa (or adj. of his गदा, meaning ‘decorated with a hundred bells’ ?). Described as large (विपुला), of great strength (महाशक्ति); when Vibhīṣaṇa was struck by Prahasta with a गदा, he took up his Śataghaṇṭā गदा and after reciting मन्त्रस् over it (अभिमन्त्र्य), threw it on Prahasta's head; the गदा, falling swiftly with the rear of a lightning, cut off the head of Prahasta 3. 270. 2-4. [See Śataghaṇṭā1]
शरवर्ष: Śaravarṣa nt.: Name of a missile (so called because it produced, when released, a shower of arrows ?). Used, among other missiles (अस्त्रपूग 3. 163. 31) by Arjuna against Kirāta (Śiva); Śiva swallowed all those अस्त्रस् (जग्रास … तानि सर्वाण्य् अस्त्राणि) 3. 163. 32. [See Śarolbaṇa]
शरोल्बण: Śarolbaṇa nt.: Name of a missile (so called because it produced, when released, excessive number of arrows ?). Used, among other missiles (अस्त्रपूग 3. 163. 31) by Arjuna against Kirāta (Śiva); Śiva swallowed all those अस्त्रस् (जग्रास … तानि सर्वाण्य् अस्त्राणि) 3. 163. 32. [See Śaravarṣa].
शार्ङ्ग: Śārṅga nt.: Name of the bow of Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa (शार्ङ्गं तु वैष्णवं प्राहुः … धारयाम् आस यत् कृष्णः 5. 155. 6). A. Acquisition: In his fight against Naraka, Kṛṣṇa cut off the nooses of the demon Muru, killed him, then conquered the demon Naraka, son of Bhūmi (भौम), and brought back with him the jewelled कुण्डलस्, sixteen thousand excellent women and various jewels; he then received the best Śārṅga bow (प्रतिपेदे हृषीकेशः शार्ङ्गं च धनुर् उत्तमम्) 5. 155. 8-9. B. Des-cription: heavenly (दिव्य) 5. 155. 6; 3. 21. 24 (धनुषा दिव्येन not named); splendid (रुचिर) 3. 23. 1; best (उत्तम) 5. 155. 9; lustrous (तेजोमय) 5. 155. 6; causing fear to the army of the enemy (परसेनाभयावह) 5. 155. 6. C. Association with Kṛṣṇa: As Kṛṣṇa's bow, it is mentioned among the weapons placed on his chariot when he started from the Khāṇḍavaprastha to Dvārakā 2. 2. 12; Kṛṣṇa asked his charioteer Dāruka to place the bow (not named) in his chariot when it was to be made ready for Kṛṣṇa's eventual intervention in the war 7. 56. 32; Śārṅga bow, along with conch, disc, mace and Śakti appeared on Kṛṣṇa's different arms when he manifested his fierce form, as a great wonder, in the Sabhā of the Kauravas 5. 129. 9-10; Kṛṣṇa (and Viṣṇu) have epithets like शार्ङ्गधन्वन् 3. 120. 6; 3. 189. 30; 5. 73. 2; 5. 135. 30; 6. 61. 35; 7. 9. 71; 8. 5. 16 (शार्ङ्ग° °धन्वन्); 10. 13. 6, 9; 12. 200. 6; 13. 135. 120; 14. 52. 6; 16. 9. 14; शार्ङ्ग-धनुर्धर 6. 61. 45; शार्ङ्गरथाङ्गपाणि 6. 55. 94; शार्ङ्गगदाधर 2. 41. 33; शार्ङ्गचक्रगदाधर 2. 42. 34; 16. 4. 44; शार्ङ्गचक्रासिपाणि 12. 43. 16. D. Use: Kṛṣṇa used it in his fight with Śālva; Kṛṣṇa's arrows released from Śārṅga first failed to reach the Saubhapura of Śālva 3. 21. 18; he again released अयुतस् of arrows against Śālva from his heavenly bow 3. 21. 24; the arrows released from Śārṅga pierced the bodies of the demons in the Saubhapura and they fell down in the ocean 3. 21. 28; due to the माया of Śālva, Kṛṣṇa saw the son of Śūra (Vasudeva) falling down from the Saubha; as a result, he was confused and the Śārṅga slipped down from his hand 3. 22. 22-25; when Kṛṣṇa knew the truth, he picked up the splendid bow and shot arrows from it which cut off the heads of the enemies 3. 23. 1-2. E. Status: The Śārṅga bow of Viṣṇu counted among the only three heavenly bows of divine beings, the other two being Gāṇḍiva of Varuṇa and Vijaya of Mahendra (त्रीण्य् एवैतानि दिव्यानि धनूंषि दिविचारिणाम्) 5. 155. 5; hence the Vijaya bow obtained by Rukmin is said to be comparable with the Śārṅga 5. 155. 4.
शिबिका: Śibikā f.: Name of a weapon (शस्त्र) of Kubera. When Indra started for the fight with Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the time of the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest, Dhaneśvara (Kubera) picked up his Śibikā to help him 1. 218. 31. (According to a view cited by Nīlakaṇṭha, शिबिका means गदा। Nīlakaṇṭha's reading is गदां चैव, but he adds शिबिकाम् इति पाठे शिबिका गदेति प्राञ्चः on Bom. Ed. 2. 227. 32). [See Antardhāna2; Kaubera astra in the Addenda].
शुक: Śuka nt.: Name of a missile. One of the eight missiles known to Arjuna; enumerated by Rāma Jāmadagnya for the information of Duryodhana; Arjuna was likely to employ these missiles during the war 5. 94. 38; for the effects produced by these missiles see Akṣisaṃtarjana.
शूल: Śūla m.: A missile (अस्त्र 13. 14. 131, 136), specially related to Śiva (Rudra) but also to Naṇdi(n), and Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa). I. Missile of Śiva: Upamanyu saw Śiva together with his missiles in bodily form (मूर्तिमन्ति तथास्त्राणि सर्वतेजोमयानि च । मया दृष्टानि गोविन्द भवस्यामित-तेजसः 13. 14. 121), one of them being the one which is known as Śūla in the three worlds 13. 14. 131; hence Śiva (Rudra) has epithets like शूलपाणि 1. 44. 22; 3. 40. 34; 3. 81. 71; 3. 104. 11; 3. 163. 43; 3. 261. 54; 5. 188. 7; 7. 64. 15; 9. 31. 38; 12. 122. 34; 12. 160. 48; 12. 283. 16; 13. 14. 132, 172; 13. 15. 11; 13. 61. 45; 13. 83. 40; 13. 127. 40; 18. 4. 10; शूलपाणिन् (m. c. for शूलपाणि ?) 3. 40. 55; 4. 40. 11; 5. 49. 24; 5. 190. 4; 10. 6. 34; शूलिन् 7. 57. 35, 52; 8. 24. 46, 136, 153; 13. 1. 25; 13. 14. 131, 139; 14. 8. 3; शूलहस्त 9. 31. 40; 9. 43. 33; शूलधृक् 2. 10. 20; 3. 81. 108; 9. 37. 43; शूलभृत् 6. 58. 61; शूलधर 3. 38. 43; खड्गशूल-धर 13. 14. 151; शूलाङ्क 10. 7. 44; दीप्तशूल 7. 172. 59; त्रिशूलपाणि 3. 80. 111; 7. 173. 33; 14. 8. 25. A. Des-cription: mysterious (गुह्य) 13. 14. 131; indescribable (अनिर्देश्य) 13. 14. 136; having very sharp points (अतितीक्ष्णाग्र); very fright-ful (सुभीम); causing the opponent's hair stand on ends (लोमहर्षण), as if threat-ening him with its eye-brow knit in three wrinkles (त्रिशिखां भ्रुकुटीं कृत्वा तर्ज-मानम् इव स्थितम्) 13. 14. 135; it was like fire without smoke, black in colour, appearing like the sun risen at the time of the end of the universe; it held a serpent in hand, and hence looking like the god of Death with his पाश in hand (विधूमं सार्चिषं कृष्णं कालसूर्यम् इवोदितम् । सर्पहस्तम् … पाश-हस्तम् इवान्तकम्) 13. 14. 136. B. Strength: If released by Śūlapāṇi (Śiva) it was capable of tearing open the whole earth, or dry up the great ocean, or destroy the entire world 13. 14. 132. C. Status: It was equal or even superior to Pāśupata (तत्-(= Pāśupata) तुल्याधिकम् एव वा) 13. 14. 131. D. Use: The demon Lavaṇa, holding this Śūla in hand, killed the very strong and universal monarch Māndhātṛ, the son of Yuvanāśva 13. 14. 133-134. E. Part in the epic war: Arjuna told Vyāsa, after the death of Droṇa, that when on the battle-field he shot arrows at his enemies he saw an excellent person (पुरुषोत्तम) of fiery lustre, looking like the sun, moving in front of him with his raised burning Śūla; the person did not touch the ground with his feet and never released the Śula, but thousands of Śūlas fell out from it; the direction in which the excellent person moved, Arjuna's enemies were destroyed; thus, actually the excellent person first burnt Arjuna's enemies and Arjuna burnt them afterwards, but people thought Arjuna did it; Vyāsa told Arjuna that the excellent person was none else but Śaṅkara with his Śūla 7. 173. 3-10. II. Association with Nandi(n), one of the attendants of Śiva: Nandin waited on Śiva holding the burning Śūla, shining with its lustre (प्रगृह्य ज्वलितम् शूलं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा) 12. 274. 15; when Upamanyu saw Śiva, Nandi stood in front of Śiva having fixed his Śūla (शूलं विष्टभ्य तिष्ठन्तम्) and hence looking like another Śaṅkara 13. 14. 144. III. Association with Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa): Viṣṇu, when he on request by Brahman creat-ed दण्डनीति, is described as one having the excellent Śūla as his weapon (शूलवरायुध) 12. 122. 26 (commentator Vādirāja, however, takes it to mean as ‘one who has a weapon (चक्र) which is superior to Śūla (शूलाद् वरं श्रेष्ठं चक्रम् आयुधं यस्य, see Cr. edn. 12. 122. 24 f. n.); Viṣṇu is also called there शूल (जटा) धर 12. 122. 24; Bhīṣma, while praising Kṛṣṇa as the highest god, uses the epithet ‘bearer of Śūla’ (शूलभृत्) to describe him 13. 143. 13.
शृङ्गाटक: Śṛṅgāṭaka m.: Name of a particular arrangement of the army (व्यूह). On the eighth day of the war, when Yudhiṣṭhira pointed out to Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Mahāvyūha of the Kauravas, to counter it Dhṛṣṭadyumna arranged the Pāṇḍava army according to the Śṛṅgāṭaka vyūha; described as very fearful (सुदारुण) 6. 83. 17; great (महाव्यूह) 6. 83. 22; destroyer of the enemy's Vyūha (परव्यूहविनाशन) 6. 83. 17; at its ‘horns’ (शृङ्गेभ्यः pl.) were stationed Bhīmasena and Sātyaki with many thousands of chariot-fighters as well as horse-soldiers and foot-soldiers; at its ‘nave’ (नाभि) stood Arjuna; its ‘centre’ (मध्य), was filled by Yudhiṣṭhira, Nakula, and Sahadeva, as also by other kings fighting with bows, and their armies; they were followed (ततः पश्चात्) by Abhimanyu, Virāṭa, the five sons of Draupadī, and Ghaṭotkaca 6. 83. 16-22.
शैलास्त्र: Śailāstra nt.: Name of a missile. Described as fierce (घोर) 6. 98. 20, and mighty (महास्त्र) 3. 168. 10; when Arjuna released the Vāyavyāstra against the Trigartas, Droṇa released the Śailāstra; as a result the force of the wind abated and the directions became clear (प्रशशाम ततो वायुः प्रसन्नाश् चाभवन् दिशः) 6. 98. 20-21; Arjuna used the Śailāstra against Kirāta (Śiva) which was swallowed (जग्रास) by the latter 3. 163. 32; when the Nivātakavaca demons produced wind with their माया, Arjuna used the mighty Śaila astra to hold the speed of the wind and defeat the माया (शैलेन च महास्त्रेण वायोर् वेगम् अधारयम्) 3. 168. 10.
श्येन: Śyena m.: Name of a व्यूह (a particular way of arranging the army). Described as the king of the Vyūhas (व्यूहराज), and invincible in battle (अजय्येन संयुगे) 6. 65. 7; on the fifth day of the war, the Pāṇḍava army was arranged according to the Śyenavyūha to counter the Makaravyūha (6. 65. 4) of the Kauravas; its ‘mouth’ (मुख) was formed by Bhīmasena, ‘eyes’ (नेत्रे) by Śikhaṇḍin and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, ‘head’ (शीर्ष) by Sātyaki, ‘neck’ (ग्रीवा) by Pārtha (Arjuna), ‘left wing’ (वामपक्ष) by Drupada and his son (not named) together with a full अक्षौहिणी army, ‘right wing’ (दक्षिण पक्ष) by Kaikeya, the leader of an अक्षौहिणी army (अक्षौहिणीपतिः), at its back (पृष्ठतः) stood the sons of Draupadī and Saubhadra (Abhimanyu), and the ‘back’ (पृष्ठ) was formed by Yudhiṣṭhira with Nakula and Sahadeva 6. 65. 7-12.
शतपथ: Śatapatha nt.: Name of a Vedic text belonging to the White Yajurveda. Described as a new Veda (lit. ‘which did not exist before’) (वेदम् अपूर्वम्) 12. 306. 23; God Sūrya blessed Yājñavalkya with a boon and told him that goddess Sarasvatī, in the form of speech, would enter his body; he then asked Yājñavalkya to open his mouth (सरस्वतीह वाग्भूता शरीरं ते प्रवेक्ष्यति । ततो माम् आह भगवान् आस्यं स्वं विवृतं कुरु । ) 12. 306. 6-7; Yājñavalkya was then to promulgate the entire Śatapatha at the end of which activity his mind would seek liberation (कृत्स्नं शतपथं चैव प्रणेष्यसि द्वि-जर्षभ । तस्यान्ते चापुनर्भावे बुद्धिस् तव भविष्यति) 12. 306. 11; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 319. 11: अपुनर्भावे मोक्षे); later, Yājñavalkya meditated on Sarasvatī and when the goddess, adorned with vowels and conso-nants, flashed before him, he offered her and the god Sūrya a guest offering; he then composed with great delight the entire Śata-patha along with its secrets, and abstracts, and supplements; he taught it to his hundred pupils (ततः शतपथं कृत्स्नं सर-हस्यं ससंग्रहम् । चक्रे सपरिशेषं च हर्षेण परमेण च ॥ कृत्वा चाध्यय-नं तेषां शिष्याणां शतम् उत्तमम्) 12. 306. 16-17; Yājñavalkya embarked on this activity keeping before his mind the seed (in the form of the fifteen यजुसेस् which he had obtained from god Sun (दश पञ्च च प्राप्तानि यजूंष्य अर्कान् मयानघ 12. 306. 21) and goddess Sarasvatī, and on the strength of the authority conferred on him by god Sūrya (बीजम् एतत् पुरस्कृत्य देवीम् चैव सरस्वतीम् । सूर्यस्य चानु-भावेन प्रवृत्तो ऽहं नराधिप ॥ ) 12. 306. 22; he taught the whole of it to his pupils and established fifteen branches of learning revealed to him by Bhāskara (god Sūrya) 12. 306. 24-25; a passage to the effect that ‘if one who knows (the real significance) gives an offering as a gift in the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa it is as good as giving an offering in kindled fire’ is supposed to occur in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (शतपथे हि ब्राह्मणं भवति । अग्नौ समिद्धे स जुहोति यो विद्वान् ब्राह्मणमुखे दाना-हुतिं जुहोति) 12. 329. 8.
शतरुद्रीय: Śatarudrī̆ya1 nt.: Name of a स्तोत्र glorifying Śiva (7. 173. 103) communicated by Vyāsa to Arjuna (देवदेवस्य ते पार्थ व्याख्यातं शतरुद्रियम्) 7. 173, 101; 7. 173. 104 (शतरुद्रीयम्). A. Description: Described as winning wealth (धन्य), fame (यशस्य), long life (आयुष्य), and merit (पुण्य), and made known by the Vedas (वेदैश् च संज्ञितम्) 7. 173. 101; fulfilling all aims (सर्वार्थ-साधक), holy (पुण्य), destroying all blemi-shes (सर्वकिल्बिषनाशन), destroying all sins (सर्वपापाप्रशमन), driving away all misery and fear (सर्वदुःखभयापह) 7. 173. 102; four-fold (चतुर्विध, probably because the स्तोत्र (1) enumerates the attri-butes of Śiva (7. 173. 9-14; 20-39), (2) describes his greatness (7. 173. 15-19; 61-81; 93-100), (3) glorifies his deeds (7. 173. 40-60), and (4) gives etymologies of his names (7. 173. 82-92); but Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 202. 50: शुद्धशबलसूत्रविराट्भेदेन भगवद्रूपस्य चातुर्विअध्यात् स्तोत्रम् अप्य् अस्य चतुर्विधम्); describes the divine deeds of the high-souled Śiva (चरितं महात्मनो दिव्यम्), of help in war (साङ्ग्रामिक), and auspicious (शुभ) 7. 173. 104. B. फल-श्रुति: One who always listens to Śatarudrīya defeats all his enemies and is highly esteemed in the Rudraloka 7. 173. 103; one who recites it or, always exerting himself, listens to it, and is devoted to god Viśveśvara obtains, when god Tryambaka is pleased, all his chosen desires 7. 173. 104-105; the स्तोत्र comprises the stanzas 7. 173. 1-101.

Śatarudrī̆ya2 nt.: Name of a Vedic text (ब्रह्म) 7. 57. 71 (Vāj. Saṃ. 16 = Tai. Saṃ. 4. 5. 1-11). A. Origin: It was created by Prājā-pati at the end of his तपस् 13. 145. 5. B. Importance: Śiva was identified by Upamanyu as Śatarudriya of Yajurveda (यजुषां शतरुद्रियम्) 13. 14. 159; Vyāsa told Arjuna that in the Veda is transmitted the excellent Śatarudrīya as a means of worship of Śiva (रेदे चास्य समाम्नातं शतरुद्रीयम् उत्तमम् । … उपस्थानं महात्मनः) 7. 173. 79; Kṛṣṇa told Yudhi-ṣṭhira that the excellent Śatarudrīya was known from the Veda and that it was a means of worshipping Śiva, which became known immediately after the one known to Vyāsa (? reference to Satarudriya1 ?) (वेदे चास्य विदुर् विप्राः शतरुद्रीयम् उत्तमम् । व्यासाद् अनन्तरं यच् चाप्य् उपस्थानं महात्मनः ॥ ) 13. 146. 23. C. Des-cription: Described as ‘special knowledge’ (विज्ञान), which constitutes the high ex-cellence and the names of Śiva, obtained by Kṛṣṇa from Durvāsas (दुर्वाससः प्रसादात् ते यत् तोदा मधुसादन । अवाप्तम् इह विज्ञानम् … महाभाग्यं च यत् तस्य नामानि च महात्मनः) 13. 145. 1-2. D. Use: Kṛṣṇa recited it every morning with folded hands 13. 145. 4; it was used to worship Rudra-Śiva on various occasions: (1) the gods gathered at Dakṣa's sacrifice tried to pacify enraged Rudra by reciting with folded hands the Śatarudrīya 13. 145. 21; (2) when different gods praised Śiva (called परं ब्रह्म) with स्तोत्रस्, Indra praised him with the excellent Śatudrīya 13. 14. 147; (3) Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, who knew the Veda, touched water, folded their hands, and worshipped the two Nāgas protecting the bow and arrow of Śiva, and recited the Śata-rudrīya in praise of Śiva 7. 57. 71.
शल्यपर्वन्: Śalyaparvan1 nt.: Name of the 74th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 59, 33, 70. Reterred to in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 148; related to the अध्यायस् 9. 1-16 (Śalya-vadhaparvan).

Śalyaparvan2 nt.: Name of the 9th पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārara 1. 2. 173, 174, 176. Described as wonderful (अद्भुत) 1. 2. 176, full of import (अर्थवत्) 1. 2. 176, having varied topics (विचित्रार्थ) 1. 2. 173; its अध्यायस् are said to describe many events (बहुवृत्तान्ताः) 1. 2. 177; the contents of the पर्वन् are summarized as follows: at the death of the excellent hero (Karṇa), the king of the Madras (Śalya) became the leader; there occurred many chariot battles (during his leadership) which are described at various places (वृत्तानि रथयुद्धानि कीर्त्-यन्ते यत्र भागशः); many principal Kuru warriors met with death; Śalya was killed by Dharmarāja; the fierce duel with maces also occurred in that पर्वन्; the holiness of the river Sarasvatī and of the तीर्थस् is described in it 1. 2. 173-175; those expert in counting numbers (संख्याविशारद) had counted its अध्यायस् to be fifty-nine 1. 2. 176 (actually the critical edition has sixty-four अध्यायस् 9. 1-64); the sage (Vyāsa) composed three thousand two hundred and twenty श्लोकस् for this पर्वन् 1. 2. 177.
शान्तिपर्वन्: Śāntiparvan nt.: Name of the 12th पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 64, 196, 197. Described as one which enhances wisdom (बुद्धिवर्धन) 1. 2. 196, and one which is liked by intelligent persons (प्राज्ञजनप्रिय) 1. 2. 199; it has three sub-पर्वन्स्: Rājadharma, Āpaddharma, and Mokṣadharma (शान्तिपर्व ततो यत्र राजधर्मानुकीर्तनम् । आपद्धर्मश् च पर्वोक्तं मोक्षधर्मस् ततः परम् । ) 1. 2. 64; these धर्मस् were expounded by Bhīṣma, lying on the bed of arrows (शान्ति-पर्वणि धर्माश् च व्याख्यातः शरतल्पि-काः) to Yudhiṣṭhira who felt dejected as he was responsible for the deaths of fathers, brothers, sons, kinsmen and relatives 1. 2. 196-197; the पर्वन् has 339 अध्यायस् and it is reported that it has 14525 stanzas 1. 2. 199-200. [See Āpaddharma, Mokṣadharma, Rājadharma]
शिशुपालवध: Śiśupālavadha m.: Name of the 26th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 41, 33, 70. The incident is mentioned while listing the contents of the Sabhāparvan 1. 2. 99; it is referred to in Sūta's summary of the events made for the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest as ‘where (was killed) the arrogant king of the Cedis’ (घातयित्वा … चैद्यं च बलगर्वितम्) 1. 1. 86; related to the अध्यायस् 2. 37-42.
श्येनकपोतीय: Śyenakapotīya nt.: Name of an उपा-ख्यान। Listed in the contents of the Āraṇyaka-parvan 1. 2. 115; in it Indra, Agni and Dharma put king Śibi to test (ततः श्येनक-पोतीयम् उपाख्यानम् अनन्तरम् । इन्द्रो ऽग्निर् यत्र धर्मश् च अजिज्ञासञ् शिबिं नृ-पम् ॥ ) 1. 2. 115; (actually in the narrative only Indra and Agni appear and the two put Śibi to test regarding his steadfastness in धर्म (इन्द्रो ऽहम् अस्मि धर्मज्ञ कपोतो हव्यवाड् अयम् । जिज्ञासमानौ धर्मे त्वाम् यज्ञवाटम् उपागतौ ॥ )) 3. 131. 28); related to the अध्याय 3. 131 (also 3. 130. 18-20).
श्राद्धपर्वन्: Śrāddhaparvan nt.: Name of the 82nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 62, 33, 70. In it the funeral rites of the Kurus were performed (कुरूणाम् और्ध्वदेहिकम्) 1. 2. 62; alluded to in the listing of the contents of the Strīparvan as one in which Yudhiṣṭhira got the bodies of the kings cremated according to the rites (राज्ञां तानि शरीराणि दाहयाम् आस शास्त्रतः) 1. 2. 193; related to the अध्याय 11. 26.
शतभिषज्: Śatabhiṣaj m.: Name of a नक्षत्र। Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that by giving gift of fragrant substances along with अगुरु and sandal wood one went after death to the world of the Apsarases and acquired permanent fragrances (गन्धाञ् शतभिषग्योगे दत्त्वा सागुरुचन्दनान् । प्राप्नोत्य् अप्सरसां लोकान् प्रेत्य गन्-धांश् च शाश्वतान्) 13. 63. 30. [See Vāruṇa]
शनैश्चर: Śanaiścara m.: Name of the planet Saturn, son of the Sun (सूर्यपुत्र 6. 3. 14; 12. 337. 52). A. Description: sharp (तीक्ष्ण) 5. 141. 7; very fierce (महाघोर) 6. 100. 20; having great lustre (महाद्युति) 5. 141. 7; blazing (प्रज्वलित) 6. 3. 25. B. Importance: Nārāyaṇa told the sage Apa-rāntatama(s) that in the Vaivasvata Man-vantara (12. 337. 41) Śanaiścara, the son of Sūrya, will be the great Manu (शनैश्-चरः सूर्यपुत्रो भविष्यति मनुर् महान् । तस्मिन् मन्वन्तरे चैव) 12. 337. 52; Śanaiścara, along with the other planets, visits the सभा of Brahman (2. 11. 20); mentioned in the Daivatavaṃśa (13. 151. 12). C. Name of Sūrya: Śanaiścara appears as the 31st name in the list of a hundred names of Sūrya taught by Dhau-mya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 20. D. Omens: Among the bad omens observed by Vyāsa before the war and reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra there was one according to which the planet Śanaiścara was afflicting the constellation Rohiṇī (रोहिणीं पीडयन्न् एष स्थितो राजञ् शनैश्चरः) 6. 2. 32; but in another state-ment Vyāsa said that Sūryaputra (i. e. Śanaiścara) was afflicting the constellation Bhāgya i. e. the Uttarā Phalgunī (भाग्यं नक्षत्रम् आक्रम्य सूर्यपुत्रेण पीड्यते) 6. 3. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 14: भगं नक्षत्रं पूर्वाफल्गुनी श्रुति-मते तूत्तरा फल्गुनी); still according to another observation of Vyāsa the two blaz-ing planets Bṛhaspati and Śanaiścara were stationed near the two Viśākhā stars and had remained there for a year (संवत्सर-स्थायिनौ च ग्रहौ प्रज्वलिताव् उभौ । विशाखयोः समीपस्थौ बृहस्पतिशनैश्-चरौ ॥ ) 6. 3. 25 (for Nī.'s comm. see Bṛhaspati); (2) According to one of the bad omens observed by Karṇa and reported to Kṛṣṇa, Śanaiścara was afflicting the con-stellation Prājāpatya, i. e. Rohiṇī and as a result was afflicting the living beings all the more (प्राजापत्यं हि नक्षत्रं ग्रहस् तीक्ष्णो महाद्युतिः । शनैश्चरः पीडयति पीडयन् प्राणिनो ऽधिकम्) 5. 141. 7. D. Simile: (1) Śalya, fighting with Yudhi-ṣṭhira, looked like Śanaiścara in the vicinity of Candramas 9. 15. 10; (2) Ārjuni (Abhimanyu) and Citrasena who came close to each other in a duel looked like the planets Budha and Śanaiścara in the sky 6. 100. 20; (3) Rāvaṇa approaching Sītā looked like Śanaiścara moving near Rohiṇī 3. 265. 6.
शिशुमार: Śiśumāra m.: Designation of a group of stars (having the shape of a dolphin), occurs in the name of a town (?), a direction (?) The kings and the Brāhmaṇas who came to attend the स्वयंवर of Draupadī went to Śiśumārapura and took residence there (ब्राह्मणाश् च महाभागाः … शिशुमार-पुरं प्राप्य न्यविशंस् ते च पार्थिवाः) 1. 176. 14-15 (Nī., who reads शिशुमार-शिरः प्राप्य observes on Bom. Ed. 1. 185. 16: शिशुमारो जलजन्तुः तदाकारस् तारा-समूहात्मको विष्णुः तस्य शिरःप्रदेशे ऐशान्यां दिशि).
शुक्र: Śukra1 m.: Name of the planet Venus, also called Bhārgava (7. 143. 30). A. Description: lustrous (तेजस्विन्) 12. 278. 5. B. History: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira once asked Bhīṣma how Uśanas of im-perishable lustre became Śukra and how he acquired prosperity (कथं चाप्य् उशना प्राप शुक्त्रत्वम् अमरद्युतिः । ऋद्धिं स च कथं प्राप्तः) 12. 278. 4 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 289. 5 explains शुक्रत्वं अस् शुक्रोत्पन्नत्वम्, cf. स विनिष्-क्रम्य शिश्नेन शुक्रत्वम् अभिपेदिवान् 12. 278. 32); Yudhiṣṭhira also asked Bhīṣma why does Śukra not move through the middle of the sky (न याति च स तेजस्वी मध्येन नभसः कथम्) 12. 278. 5; 12. 278. 32 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 289. 5: तस्य आकाशगतिः कुतः कुण्ठितेत्य् अर्थः । सप्तर्षिवद् द्वीरूपेण स्थितस्य शुक्रस्य भूस्थमूर्तिविषयक एवायं प्रश्नो न भचक्रस्थमूर्तिविषयः तेन यथा भौ-मानां वसिष्ठादीनां स्वर्गे ऽपि गतिर् अस्ति नैवं भौमस्य शुक्रस्यास्तीति गम्यते । ); (2) Parāśara told Janaka that Uśanas be-came Śukra by propitiating Devadeva (Śiva); and by praising Devī (Umā) he, covered with lustre, delights in the sky (गतः शुक्रत्वम् उशना देवदेवप्रसादनात् । देवीं स्तुत्वा तु गगने मोदते तेजसा वृतः) 12. 281. 14 (a reference to 12. 278. 13-37); (3) Planet Śukra is the son of Kavi (शुक्रः कविसुतो ग्रहः) 1. 60. 40 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 66. 42: शुक्रो ग्रह-त्वाद् एव लोकानां प्राणयात्रायां वर्षा-वर्षादिकार्ये नियुक्तः) C. Importance: (1) Śukra, along with other planets, visits the सभा of Brahman 2. 11. 20; (2) finds place in the Daivatavaṃśa 13. 151. 12. D. Name of Sūrya: Śukra appears as the 23rd name in the list of the 108 names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 19. E. Auspicious: (1) When Dhṛtarāṣṭra heard that the planet Śukra and Sūrya both together were favourable to the sons of Kuntī for their victory in war he did not hope to win (यदाश्रौषं शुक्र-सूर्यौ च युक्तौ कौन्तेयानाम् अनुलोमौ जयाय … तदा नासंसे विजयाय संजय ॥ ) 1. 1. 129; (2) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that in wars, victory was on that side for which wind, Sūrya and the planet Śukra were favourable; if they all were simultaneously present, each time the former was stronger than the latter (यतो वायुर् यतः सूर्यो यतः शुक्रस् ततो जयः । पूर्वं पूर्वं ज्याय एषां संनिपाते युधिष्ठिर 12. 101. 17. F. Bad effect: While Śukra is in conjunction with the two Proṣṭhapadās it has wealth (as Kubera, the lord of riches, also has); Śukra in that position takes away from men whatever they have earned according to their desires 5. 112. 3 (for citation and Nī.'s comm. see Pūrvā Bhādrapadā); (for Śukra as a great sage and perfect in योग depriv-ing also Kubera of his wealth see 12. 278. 7-9). G. Omens: Among the bad omens noticed by the Vyāsa before the war one was related to Śukra's ascending the Pūrva Proṣṭhapada and then, after going over to the Uttara Proṣṭhapada, both looking back at the Pūrva Proṣṭhapada 6. 3. 14 (for citation see Uttarā Bhādrapadā). H. Similes: (1) The battle between Drupada and Jaya-dratha, delightful to the spectators (ईक्षितृ-प्रीतिजननम्), was like the one between Śukra and Aṅgāraka 6. 43. 54; (2) Droṇa and Arjuna met in battle like Budha and Śukra in the sky (नभस्तले) 6. 97. 57; (3) The battle between Prativindhya and Duḥśāsana was like the one between Budha and Bhārgava (Śukra) in a cloudless sky (व्यपेतजलदे व्योम्नि) 7. 143. 30; (4) Arjuna, with Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki by his side in the chariot, looked like the darkness-destroying Śaśin with Budha and Śukra 7. 60. 20. [For Śukra also see Section 1. 7]

Śukra2 m.: Name of the month Jyaiṣṭha, mentioned mostly along with Śuci. Similes: (1) When Bhīma strode fast, wind generated by the speed of his thighs blew as it does at the advent of the months Śukra (Jyaiṣṭha) and Śuci (Āṣāḍha) (प्र-ववाव् अनिलो राजञ् शुचिशुक्रागमे यथा) 1. 138. 1. (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 151. 2: शुचिशुक्रागमे ज्येष्ठाषाढयोः समये); (2) Duryodhana, burning with anger after witnessing the Rājasūya of the Pāṇḍavas, was drying up as does scanty water at the advent of Jyaiṣṭha and Āṣāḍha (शुचिशुक्रागमे काले शुष्ये तोयम् इवाल्पकम्) 2. 43. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 47. 24: शुचिशुक्रौ ज्येष्ठा-षाढौ तयोर् आगमे ग्रीष्मर्तौ); (3) Arjuna, tormenting his enemies with his Gāṇḍīva bow drawn full circle and his arrows issuing from it like hot rays, shone like the haloed sun in the middle of the months Jyaiṣṭha and Āṣāḍha (तपन् रिपून् अर्जुनभास्करो बभौ । शरोग्ररश्मिः शुचिशुक्रमध्यगो यथैव सूर्यः परि-वेषगस् तथा ॥ ) 8. 57. 57. [See Jyeṣṭhā-mūla]
शुचि: Śuci m.: Name of the month Āṣāḍha, mentioned mostly with Śukra2. Simile: Droṇa, showering (arrows) like hail stones frightened his enemies as does the roaring and windly Parjanya at the end of the month Śuci (i. e. at the end of Āṣāḍha, or at the end of the hot season ?) (नान-द्यमानः पर्जन्यः सानिलः शुचिसंक्षये । अश्मवर्षम् इवावर्षत् परेषाम् आवहद् भयम् ॥ ) 7. 13. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 14. 5: शुचिसंक्षये ग्रीष्मान्ते); for other similes, see Śukra2. [See Āṣāḍha]
श्याम: Śyāma adj.: Designation of the planet Rāhu. [See Rāhu]

Śyāma m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: One of the seven moun-tains of the Śākadvīpa, located in its north (उत्तरेण तु राजेन्द्र श्यामो नाम महा-गिरिः) 6. 12. 17; the distance in योजनस् between the seven mountains doubles as one progresses from the one to the other (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 12. 22; the name of the Varṣa of Śyāma mountain is Maṇīcaka 6. 12. 24. B. Des-cription: Big mountain (महागिरि) 6. 12. 17; all the seven mountains of the Śākadvīpa are described as adorned with jewels and mines of precious stones (तथैव पर्वता राजन् सप्तात्र मणिभूषिताः । रत्नाकराः) 6. 12. 13. C. Characteristic: Owing to the existence of Śyāma (black) mountain in Śākadvīpa the people there are black in colour; the reason for the black colour of the mountain as told by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, is that god Kṛṣṇa lives on that mountain and the colour of the mountain has turned black due to Kṛṣṇa's colour (श्यामो नाम महा-गिरिः । यतः श्यामत्वम् आपन्नाः प्रजा जनपदेश्वर ॥ … श्यामो यस्मात् प्रवृत्तो वै तत् ते वक्ष्यामि भारत । आस्ते ऽत्र भग-वान् कृष्णस् तत्कान्त्या श्यामतां गतः ॥ ) 6. 12. 17, 20.
शवण: Śavaṇa m.: Name of a constellation. A. Importance: Menakā, while descri-bing to Indra the exploits of Viśvāmitra, said that he, enraged by the abundance of constellations, started to create, in addition to the existing galaxies of constellations, counter-constellations starting with Śravaṇa (अति नक्षत्रवंशांश् च क्रुद्धो नक्षत्र-संपदा । प्रति श्रवणपूर्वाणि नक्षत्राणि ससर्ज यः ॥ ) 1. 65. 34. B. Auspi-cious: Balarāma left for his तीर्थयात्रा under the constellation Puṣya and returned, after forty days, under the constellation Śravaṇa (चत्वारिंशद् अहान्य् अद्य द्वे च मे निःसृतस्य वै । पुष्येण संप्रयातो ऽस्मि श्रवणे पुनर् आगतः ॥ ) 9. 33. 5 (see the Editor's note on the stanza Cr. Ed. Vol. 11, p. 489). C. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave under the constellation Śravaṇa a gift of a woolen blanket with a piece of a cloth attached from inside, he could reach to all the worlds which remained unconcealed from him (?) in a bright con-veyance (श्रवणे कम्बलं दत्त्वा वस्त्रान्-तरितम् एव च । श्वेतेन याति यानेन सर्वान् लोकान् असंवृतान्) 13. 63. 28; (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by performing a काम्य श्राद्ध under Śravaṇa one obtained excellent condition after death (प्रेत्य गच्छेत् परां गतिम्) 13. 89. 11. D. Omens: (1) According to one of the bad omens for the armies noticed by Vyāsa before the war, the planet Bṛhaspati was taking retrograde step under Śravaṇa (मघास्व् अङ्गारको वक्रः श्रवणे च बृहस्पतिः) 6. 3. 13; (2) According to another omen noticed by Vyāsa the planet Mars, after taking repeated retrograde steps (under Maghā ?), had returned to Brahma-rāśi and remained steady in Śravaṇa 6. 3. 17 (for the citation and Nī.'s comm. see Bra-hmarāśi p. 260 above). [See Brahmarāśi, Vaiṣṇava and Śraviṣṭhā]
श्रविष्ठा: Śraviṣṭhā f.: Name of a constellation. According to Brahmadeva the constella-tions began with Śraviṣṭhā (श्रविष्ठादीनि ऋक्षाणि) 14. 44. 2 (व्। ल्। श्रवणादीनि, see Śravaṇa above, section A).
श्रावण: Śrāvaṇa m.: Name of a month. Aṅgiras had told Bhīṣma that if one remained controlled and spent the month of Śrāvaṇa taking food only once a day he was given the honour of अभिषेक (ceremonial bath ?) wherever he went and became the prosperer of his kinsmen (श्रावणं नियतो मासम् एकभक्तेन यः क्षपेत् । यत्र तत्राभिषेकेण युज्यते ज्ञातिवर्धनः ॥ ) 13. 109. 26.
श्रीपञ्चमी: Śrīpañcamī f.: Name of the fifth day (of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha). When Devasenā received Skanda for her husband, Lakṣmī, in person, attended on him; since Skanda was chosen by Śri (Lakṣmī) on the fifth day (of the month of Māgha), that day became known as Śrīpañcamī. (यदा स्कन्दः पतिर् लब्धः शाश्वतो देवसेनया । तदा तम् आश्रयल् लक्ष्मीः स्वयं देवी शरीरिणी ॥ श्रीजुष्टः पञ्चमीं स्कन्दस् तस्माच् छ्रीपञ्चमी स्मृता) 3. 218. 48-49.
शक्रस्य: Śakrasya tīrtham nt.: See Kumārikā-ṇāṃ tīrtham.
शक्रावर्त: Śakrāvarta m.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who satisfies according to the rites gods and manes (by giving offerings) is glori-fied in the world of the meritorious (शक्रा-वर्ते च तर्पयन् । देवान् पितॄंश् च विधिवत् पुण्यलोके महीयते ॥ ) 3. 82. 25.
शङ्खतीर्थ: Śaṅkhatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī (तत्र तीर्थं सरस्वत्याः) 9. 36. 24; Balarāma reached it from Gargasrotas 9. 36. 16, 19. B. Description: Purifying (पावन), famous in the worlds (लोक-विश्रुत) 9. 36. 24; a तीर्थ of those who get success (तीर्थे यशस्विनाम्) 9. 36. 25. C. Characteristic: The famous Mahāśaṅkha tree on the river Sarasvatī situated near it 9. 36. 20 (see Mahāśaṅkha). D. Epic event: Balarāma gave there vessels of copper-iron and various kinds of garments to Brāh-maṇas and worshipped them; he was honoured there by ascetics (दत्त्वा … ताम्रायसानि भाण्डानि वस्त्राणि विविधानि च); from there he went to Dvaitavana 9. 36. 25-26.
शङ्खिनी: Śaṅkhinī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Devī (देव्यास् तीर्थे); a pilgrim, by bathing there, gets excellent form (लभते रूपम् उत्तमम्) 3. 81. 41.
शतकुम्भा: Śatakumbhā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 18, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā); also listed by Mārka-ṇḍeya among rivers which are famous as mothers of the sacrificial hearths (धिष्ण्या-नां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed 3. 212. 21 (for Nī. see Kapilā); by visiting it one is glorified in heaven (अभिगम्य नर-श्रेष्ठ स्वर्गलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 9.
शतद्रु: Śatadru f.: Name of a river; once referred to as Śatadrukanadī (8. 30. 21). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; flowing from the Himavant (हैमवती) 1. 167. 8; the Bāhlīka (or the Āraṭṭa) country lies between the five rivers and Sindhu 8. 30. 11; the five rivers are Śatadru, Vipāśā, Irāvatī, Candrabhāgā and Vitastā 8. 30. 35-36; one has to cross the rivers Śatadru and Irāvatī to reach the Bāhlīka country (सा नूनम् … माम् अनुस्मरती शेते बाह्लिकम् … ॥ शतद्रु-कनदीं तीर्त्वा तां च रम्याम् इरावतीम् । गत्वा स्वदेशम् द्रक्ष्यामि) 8. 30. 20-21. B. Description: Flowing from the Himavant (हैमवती) 1. 167. 8; having ferocious crocodiles (चण्डग्राहवती) 1. 167. 8; ex-cellent river (सरिद्वरा) 1. 167. 9; all the rivers listed by Umā are described as auspici-ous (शिवाः), most holy (पुण्यतमाः) 13. 134. 22; having waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; ex-cellent rivers (सरिद्वराः), (सरितां वराः), (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाः) 13. 134. 14, 19, 22; flow-ing to the ocean (सागरगमाः) 13. 134. 21; expert in the knowledge of the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 12. 134. 19; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Name explained: When Vasiṣṭha jumped into a river to end his life, the river, feeling him like fire, ran into hundred streams; hence the river came to be known as Śatadru (सा तम् अग्निसमं विप्रम् अनुचिन्त्य सरिद्-वरा । शतधा विद्रुता यस्माच् छतद्रुर् इति स्मृता) 1. 167. 9. D. Past events: (1) Vasiṣṭha, grieved over the death of his sons, made attempts to end his life; once he threw himself in a river which later came to be known as Śatadru 1. 166. 39; 1. 167. 8; (2) One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93. E. Impor-tance: (1) One of the rivers who wait up-on Śiva for his bath (उपस्पर्शनहेतोस् त्वा समीपस्था उपासते) 13. 134. 12; (2) Umā wanted to consult rivers, one of them being Śatadru, on स्त्रीधर्म before expound-ing it to Śiva 13. 134. 13, 20; Umā thus wanted to honour them 13. 134. 14, 25; (3) One of the rivers who, in bodily form (2. 9. 21), wait on Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 19; (4) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 14, 2.
शतबला: Śatabalā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
शतशृङ्ग: Śataśṛṅga m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Beyond the Gandha-mādana and Haṃsakūṭa mountains (प्रय-यौ गन्धमादनम् … हंसकूटम् अतीत्य च) 1. 110. 43, 45. B. Description: King of mountains (शैलराज) 1. 111. 5, 10. C. Characteristic: Siddhas and Cāraṇas lived there 1. 111. 1; so also Brāhmaṇas (विप्राः) 1. 115. 21, sages (ऋषयः) 1. 113. 3, and ascetics (तापसाः) 1. 111. 5, (तप-स्विनां … शतशृङ्गनिवासिनाम्) 1. 114. 37; 8. 48. 11; 1. 110. 45; D. Epic events: (1) Forsaking all enjoyments Pāṇḍu repaired to this mountain 1. 117. 20; when he, with his two wives, reached Śata-śṛṅga he became an ascetic (शतशृङ्गे … तापसः समपद्यत) 1. 110. 45; there he practised austerities of a high order (तत्रापि तपसि श्रेष्ठे वर्तमानः) 1. 111. 1; when Pāṇḍu, with his wives, wanted to go further northwards from this mountain he was dis-suaded by the ascetics who lived there 1. 111. 5, 10; (2) When the Pāṇḍavas were born, the Brāhmaṇas who lived on Śataśṛṅga gave them names (नामानि चक्रिरे तेषां शत-शृङ्गनिवासिनः) 1. 115. 19; (3) A week after Arjuna's birth an invisible voice from sky on top of Śataśṛṅga told Kuntī the future heroic deeds of Arjuna (इत्य् अन्तरिक्षे शतशृङ्ग-मूर्ध्नि तपस्विनां शृण्वतां वाग् उवाच) 8. 48. 6-11 (a reference to 1. 114. 28-36); the ascetics living on Śataśṛṅga were delighted to hear the incorporeal voice which were the words spoken by Vāyu in sky (वाग् उवाचा-शरीरिणी । … उक्तवान् वायुर् आकाशे … ।वाचम् उच्चारिताम् … निशम्य तपस्विनाम् । बभूव परमो हर्षः शतशृङ्गनिवासिनाम् ॥ ) 1. 114. 28, 37; (4) Kuntī told the Pāṇḍavas when they started for the forest that if she had known what was in their store she, after the death of Pāṇḍu, would not have returned from Śataśṛṅga to Hāstinapura 2. 70. 17; (5) One of the mountains seen by Arjuna when he, with Kṛṣṇa, went at night to Śiva's abode to obtain his Pāśupata 7. 57. 16-17, 28. E. Past event: In the sacrifices of the ancestors of Sulabhā, for the चयन, the mountains Droṇa, Śataśṛṅga and Vakra-dvāra were used as bricks with the help of Maghavant (मम सत्रेषु पूर्वेषां चिता मघवता सह) 12. 308. 183 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 320. 82: द्रोणादयः पर्वताः मम पूर्वेषां सत्रेषु मघवता सह चिताः चयने इष्टकास्थाने निवेशिता इत्य् अर्थः).
शतसहस्रक: Śatasahasraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Sāhasraka तीर्थ; both the तीर्थस् were famous in the world (द्वे-तीर्थे लोकविश्रुते) 3. 81. 137; by bathing there one got the fruit of giving a thousand cows, and his gifts and fasts would give him a thousandfold benefit (दानं वाप्य् उपवासो वा सहस्रगुणितं भवेत्) 3. 81. 138.
शतसाहस्रिक: Śatasāhasrika nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the river Gomatī, near Rāmatīrtha 3. 82. 66-67; by bathing in it (उपस्पर्शनम्) and by controlling oneself and taking limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 82. 67.
शतावरी: Śatāvarī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
शर्यातिवन: Śaryātivana nt.: Name of a forest. One of the regions over which Arjuna flew when he, with Kṛṣṇa, went during the night to see Śiva to get his Pāśupata 7. 57. 16-17, 28.
शलु: Śalu f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
शशयान: Śaśayāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Located on the river Sara-svatī (सरस्वत्याम् … स्नायन्ते) 3. 80. 121. B. Description: Described as difficult to reach (दुर्लभ) 3. 80. 120. C. Chara-cteristic: Lotuses in this तीर्थ are concealed since they appear in the form of rabbits (शशरूपप्रतिच्छन्नाः पुष्करा यत्र भारत) 3. 80. 120 (this explains the name of the तीर्थ ?). D. Holiness: People bathe (in this तीर्थ) on Sarasvatī all the year round (सरस्वत्यां महाराज अनु संवत्सरं हि ते । स्नायन्ते); if one bathes there on the full moon day of the Kārtika month one shines always like the moon and in addition gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows (वृत्तां वै कार्तिकीं सदा ॥ तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र द्योतते शशिवत् सदा । गोसहस्रफलं चैव प्राप्नुयात्) 3. 80. 121-122.
शशिकान्ता: Śaśikāntā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
शाक: Śāka m.: Name of a tree of the Śāka-dvīpa. Described as famous (विख्यात) and a big tree (महाद्रुम); it is situated in the middle of that Dvīpa (तस्य मध्ये महाद्रुमः ॥ शाको नाम महाराज तस्य द्वीपस्य मध्यगः । ) 6. 12. 25-26.
शाकम्भरी: Śākambharī f.: Name of a place (स्थानम्) sacred to goddess Śākambharī. A. Description: Place of the famous goddess, known in the three worlds as Śākam-bharī; very difficult of access (देव्याः स्था-नं सुदुर्लभम् । शाकम्भरीति विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता) 3. 82. 11. B. Holi-ness: One who practises austerities and is composed (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः) should visit Śākambharī and stay there for three nights; pure and controlled (नियतः शुचिः) he should eat only vegetables; he thereby obtains the fruit of living only on vegetables for twelve years; this happens by the will of the goddess (शाकाहारस्य यत् सम्यग् वर्-षैर् द्वादशभिः फलम् । तत् फलं तस्य भवात् देव्याश् छन्देन) 3. 82. 14-15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 18: छन्देन इच्छया).
शालिशूर्प: Śāliśūrpa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A तीर्थ of Śālihotra (शालिहोत्रस्य शालि-शूर्पे); by bathing there according to the prescribed rites one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 90.
शालूकिनी: Śālūkinī f.: Name of a river (?). Daśāśvamedhika तीर्थ is situated there 3. 81. 11.
शिवा: Śivā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
शिवोद्भेद: Śivodbheda m.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the three places—the other two being Camasa and Nāgodbheda—where the river Sarasvatī reappears after disappearing at Vinaśana on a desert place (गच्छत्य् अन्तर्हिता यत्र (i. e. विनशने) मरुपृष्ठे सरस्वती । चमसे च शिवोद्भेदे नागोद्भेदे च दृश्यते ॥ ) 3. 80. 118; by bathing there one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 80. 119.
शीघ्रा: Śīghrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 28, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
शीतवन: Śītavana nt.: Name of a forest. There is a तीर्थ in this forest; it is great and one similar to it is difficult to find elsewhere (तीर्थं तत्र महाराज महद् अन्यत्र दुर्लभम्); one who is controlled and takes limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) should go there; it purifies some people by its mere sight, others by prostration (?) (पुनाति दर्शनाद् एव दण्डेनैकं नराधिप); (however Arjunamiśra: एकम् इति तृतीयार्थे द्वितीया; cf. Cr. Edn. fn. to st. 49), and still others by sprinkling water on their hair (केशान् अभ्युक्ष्य वै तस्मिन् पूतो भवति भारत) 3. 81. 48-49.
शुक्तिमती: Śuktimatī f.: Name of a river. A.
