Location: It flows by the city of king Vasu Uparicara (पुरोपवाहिनीं तस्य नदीं शुक्तिमतीम्) 1. 57. 32; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhārata-varṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 33, 13. B. Description: All the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Past event: The mountain Kolāhala, who had gained con-sciousness, obstructed the course of the river Śuktīmatī as he was enamoured of her (अरौत्सीच् चेतनायुक्तः कामात् कोलाहलः किल); Vasu struck the mountain with his foot and the river gushed forth from the hole produced by the stroke of the foot; the mountain begot on the river two children—a male and a female; this was reported to the king by the river; the king, delighted by her release, made the male chief his child of army and married the female 1. 57. 32-35.

Śuktimatī, Śuktisāhvayā f.: Name of a town, the capital of the Chedi country, hence referred to as Cedipura (2. 40. 14), Cedipurī (3. 65. 6), Cedirājapurī (3. 62. 20). A. Description: Delightful (रम्या) 3. 23. 47; 3. 65. 6; 14. 84. 2. B. Epic events: (1) Dhṛṣṭaketu, king of the Chedi country, after meeting the Pāṇḍavas, took his sister (Kareṇumatī, wife of Nakula) with him and left for the town Śuktimatī (धृष्टकेतुः स्वसारं च समादायाथ चेदिराट् । जगाम  … रम्यां शुक्तिमतीम् पुरीम्) 3. 23. 47 (Nī. on 3. 22. 50: स्वसारं करेणुमतीं नकुलभार्याम्); (2) The sacrificial horse for the Aśvemedha of Yudhiṣṭhira reached Śuktisāhvayā, the town of the Cedis (आस-साद पुरीं रम्यां चेदीनां शुक्तिसाह्व-याम्) 14. 84. 2; (3) Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa once went to Cedipura to meet the sister of their father (ततश् चेदिपुरं प्राप्तौ सं-कर्षणजनार्दनौ) 2. 40. 14. C. Events from Nala story: (1) The people of Cedi-rājapurī saw Damayantī entering their town after she was deserted by Nala (ददृशुः पुरवासिनः ॥ प्रविशन्तीं … चेदिराजपुरीं तदा) 3. 62. 19-20; (2) A Brāhmaṇa, called Sudeva, reached Cedipurī in search of Damayantī (ततश् चेदिपुरीं रम्यां सुदेवो नाम वै द्विजः । विचिन्वानो ऽथ वै-दर्भीम्) 3. 65. 6. [For river Śuktimatī, see Vol. I. 457]
शुक्तिमत्: Śuktimant m.: Name of a mountain. Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven principal mountain ranges (कुलपर्वताः) of the Bhāratavarṣa, there are many other thousands of mountains near them (तेषां सहस्रशो राजन् पर्वतास् तु समीपतः) 6. 10. 10-11.
शुक्तिमन्त्: Śuktimant m.: Name of a mountain. Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven principal mountain ranges (कुलपर्वताः) of the Bhāratavarṣa, there are many other thousands of mountains near them (तेषां सहस्रशो राजन् पर्वतास् तु समीपतः) 6. 10. 10-11.
शुभस्कन्ध: Śubhaskandha m.: Name of a moun-tain. One of the mountains described by Brahman to the sages as kings of mountains (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 5.
शूर्पारक: Śūrpāraka m., nt.: Name of a place and a तीर्थ; also called once Sūrpāraka (13. 26. 47). A. Location: In the south (दक्षिण-स्याम्) 3. 86. 1; (दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; in the south, along the seacoast (पारं समुद्रस्य दक्षिणे) 12. 49. 58; (शूर्पा-रकं देशं सागरस्य) 12. 49. 59; on the western border of the earth (सो ऽपरान्तं महीतलम्) 12. 49. 59; one of the तीर्थस् along the seacoast (तानि तीर्थानि च साग-रस्य) 3. 118. 8; (तेन तीर्थेन तु साग-रस्य) 3. 118. 15; Rāmatīrtha located near it (?) 3. 83. 40. B. Description: Most holy (पुण्यतम) 3. 118. 8. C. Chara-cteristic: Frequented by Jāmadagnya 3. 83. 40; there are two altars (वेदी) of Jāmadag-nya called Pāṣāṇatīrthā and Puraścandrā at Śūrpāraka 3. 86. 9. D. Holiness: By bathing in waters of Sūrpāraka and by observing fast for a fortnight one becomes a prince (उपस्पृश्य तथा सूर्पारकोदके । एकपक्षनिराहारो राजपुत्रो विधीयते) 13. 26. 47. E. Epic events: (1) Śūrpāraka was conquered by Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya 2. 28. 43; (2) Visited by the Pāṇḍavas in their तीर्थ-यात्रा 3. 118. 8; after visiting some more places, they returned to Śūrpāraka 3. 118. 14. F. Past event: When Kaśyapa asked Rāma Jāmadagnya to go to the southern sea-coast, the ocean, due to fear of Rāma, (re-ceded and) vacated space for him; that space emptied by the ocean, which was on the western border of the earth, came to be known as Śūrpāraka (ततः शूर्पारकं देशं सागरस् तस्य निर्ममे । संत्रासाज् जाम-दग्न्यस्य सो ऽपरान्तं महीतलम्) 12. 49. 59.
शृङ्ग: Śṛṅga, Śṛṅgavant, Śṛṅgin m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: To the south of Śṛṅgin and to the north of Śveta lies the Varṣa called Hairaṇvata 6. 9. 5 (according to 6. 7. 35 Hairaṇyaka); beyond Śṛṅga and to its north and up to the coast of the ocean lies the Varṣa called Airāvata (उत्तरेण तु शृङ्गस्य समुद्रान्ते जनाधिप । वर्षम् ऐरावतं नाम तस्माच् छृङ्गवतः परम्) 6. 9. 10; 6. 7. 35. B. Description: Beset with all kinds of minerals (सर्वधातु-विनद्ध) 6. 7. 3; Śṛṅgavant is one of the six mountains listed by Saṃjaya which are called mountains of precious stones (षड् एते रत्नपर्वताः); all of them stretch to-ward the east and are merged at both ends in the eastern and western oceans (प्रागा-यताः … अवगाढा ह्य् उभयतः समु-द्रौ पूर्वपश्चिमौ) 6. 7. 2; all of them are visited by the Siddhas and Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेविताः) 6. 7. 4; the distance between these mountains extends to thousands of योजनस् (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो योज-नानि सहस्रशः) 6. 7. 4; (see also the next section). C. Characteristics: (1) There are only three peaks on this mountain; one of them is full of jewels, the other is golden and wonderful, and the third is full of all kinds of precious stones and is adorned with palatial mansions (शृङ्गाणि वै शृङ्गवतस् त्रीण्य् एव मनुजाधिप । एकं मणिमयं तत्र तथैकं रौक्मम् अद्भुतम् ॥ सर्व-रत्नमयं चैकं भवनैर् उपशोभि-तम्) 6. 9. 8-9; (2) The goddess Śāṇḍilī, who is self-luminous, always lives there (तत्र स्वयंप्रभा देवी नित्यं वसति शाण्डिली) 6. 9. 9; (3) Manes haunt Śṛṅga-vant (शृङ्गवांस् तु महाराज पितॄणां प्रतिसंचरः) 6. 7. 49. D. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2.
शैलोदा: Śailodā f.: Name of a river. Flows between the mountains Meru and Mandara; there is a lovely shade of different kinds of bamboos on its banks (कीचकवेणू-नां छायां रम्याम् उपासते) 2. 48. 2.
शैशिर: Śaiśira m.: Name of a mountain (one of the ranges of Himavant). A. Location: In the north (प्रायाद् उदङ्मुखः । शैशिरं गिरिम् उद्दिश्य) 12. 314. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 327. 2: शैशिरं गिरिं हिमालयम्); near the Bhṛgu-tuṅga range 3. 163. 10. B. Characteristic: Considered extremely unshakable; hence Bhīma boasted that his arms were capable of toppling down even the Śaiśira mountain (समर्थौ पर्वतस्यापि शैशिरस्य निपा-तने) 7. 170. 48. C. Epic event: As advised by a Brāhmaṇa living at Bhṛgutuṅga, Arjuna went up the Śaiśira mountain to practise austerities (गिरिम् आरुह्य शैशिरम् । तपो ऽतप्यं महाराज); he met there a boar chased by a Kirāta (Śiva) 3. 163. 14, 17, 19 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 167. 15: शैशिरं हिममयम्); on the day following Arjuna's encounter with the Kirāta, there blew holy wind and heavenly, fresh, fragrant flowers appeared at the foot of Śaiśira (शै-शिरस्य गिरेः पादे प्रादुरासन् समन्ततः) 3. 164. 8; he saw there Indra and other gods; he received missiles from Kubera and other gods and a promise from Indra to give him all heavenly missiles at his residence; when the heavenly chariot of Indra was brought to Arjuna by Mātali, he bade farewell to Śaiśira and mounted the chariot after making a प्रदक्षिणा (of the chariot) (गिरिम् आमन्-त्र्य शैशिरम् । प्रदक्षिणम् उपावृत्य समारोहं रथोत्तमम् ॥ ) 1. 164. 9-34. D. Past event: When instructed by Janaka, Śuka flew like wind towards the north to the Śaiśira mountain to meet Vyāsa 12. 314. 2. [See Himavant]
शोण: Śoṇa m., Soṇā f.: Name of a river. A. Source and location: Listed by Saṃjaya (Śoṇā) among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drink-ing 6. 10. 28, 13; in the east; Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna crossed the rivers Gaṅgā and Śoṇa while proceeding towards the east to the Magadha country (उत्तीर्य गङ्गां शोणं च सर्वे ते प्राङ्मुखास् त्रयः … जग्मुर् मागधं क्षेत्रम्) 2. 18. 29; the river flew between Gaṇḍakīyā and Sadānīrā rivers (गण्डकीयां तथा शोणं सदानीरां त-थैव च … क्रमेणैत्य व्रजन्ति ते) 2. 18. 27; the three rivers rise on the same moun-tain (एकपर्वतके नद्यः) 2. 18. 27; its source is known as Vaṃśagulma which is also the source of Narmadā (शोणस्य नर्-मदायाश् च प्रभवे कुरुनन्दन । वंश-गुल्मे) 3. 83. 9. B. Description: All the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: (1) A pure person (शुचिः) who lives (निवसन्) at the confluence of Jyoti-rathyā and Śoṇa and satisfies manes and gods gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 83. 8; (2) By bathing (उप्स्पृश्य) at Vaṃśa-gulma, the source of Śoṇa and Narmadā, one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice 3. 83. 9; (3) Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among rivers which are declared to be mothers of fire-hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed 3. 212. 24 (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā). D. Epic event: Śoṇa was one of the rivers crossed by Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna when they left Indraprastha to go to the Magadha country 2. 18. 27, 29. E. Past event: Śoṇa is one of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95.
श्रीकुञ्ज: Śrīkuñja nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्यां तीर्थम्); one who bathes there gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 81. 91.
श्रीतीर्थ: Śrītīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who reaches there (समासाद्य) gets the best prosperity (विन्दते श्रियम् उत्तमाम्) 3. 81. 37.
श्रीपर्वत: Śrīparvata m.: Name of a mountain. Mahādeva with the goddess (Umā) lived on this mountain; god Brahman, surrounded by other gods, also lived there 3. 83. 17; a river flows along the mountain Śrīparvata; by bathing on its bank (नदीतीर उपस्पृशेत्) one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and goes to heaven 3. 83. 16; one who is pure and has controlled his mind he, by bathing in the तीर्थ Devahrada there, gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and attains highest success (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः । अश्वमेधम् अवा-प्नोति परां सिद्धिं च गच्छति) 3. 83. 18.
श्वानलोमापनयन: Śvānalomāpanayana, Śvānalomāpaha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the Śītavana (तीर्थं तत्र महाराज श्वानलोमापहं स्मृतम्) 3. 81. 48, 50; at this तीर्थ pilgrims who are ex-cellent Brāhmaṇas remove the hair of dogs by doing breath exercises (?); by purifying thus their souls they reach the highest condi-tion (यत्र विप्राः … तीर्थतत्पराः ॥ श्वा-नलोमापनयने तीर्थे भरतसत्तम । प्राणायामैर् निर्हरन्ति श्वलोमानि द्विजो-त्तमाः । पूतात्मानश् च राजेन्द्र प्रयान्ति परमां गतिम्) 3. 81. 50-51.
शङ्कुकर्णेश्वर: Śaṅkukarṇeśvara m.: Name of a holy place. Close to the famous तीर्थ called Dṛmi 3. 80. 87; wise men say that by worshipp-ing god Śaṅkukarṇeśvara (Śiva) at this place one got tenfold fruit of performing an Aśvamedha sacrifice (अश्वमेधं दश-गुणं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः) 3. 80. 87.
शतयूपाश्रम: Śatayūpāśrama m.: The आश्रम of the royal sage Śatayūpa. A. Location: In Kurukṣetra (कुरु-क्षेत्रं जगाम सः । तत्राश्रमपदं … अभिगम्य … आससाद … शतयूपम्) 15. 25. 8-9; (ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा कुरुक्षेत्रम् अवातरत्) 15. 30. 16; beyond the river Yamunā, at some distance from it (क्रमेणो-त्तीर्य यमुनां नदीम् … ॥ स ददर्शाश्र-मं दूरात् … शतयूपस्य) 15. 30. 16-17. B. Epic events: (1) When Dhṛtarāṣṭra decided to leave Hāstinapura and live in an आश्रम, he went to Kurukṣetra; there he reached the hermitage of Śatayūpa, the great king of the Kekayas (तत्राश्रम-पदं … अभिगम्य … आससाद … शतयू-पम्); with him Dhṛtarāṣṭra went to Vyāsā-śrama 15. 25. 9-11; after he was initiated by Vyāsa (स दीक्षां तत्र संप्राप्य), Dhṛtarāṣṭra returned to the आश्रम of Śatayūpa and lived there; as suggested by Vyāsa, Śatayūpa gave complete instructions to Dhṛtarāṣṭra regarding the mode of life of a forest-dweller (शतयूपाश्रमे तस्मिन् निवासम् अकरोत् तदा ॥ तस्मै सर्वं विधिं … राजाचख्यौ … । आरण्यकम् … व्यासस्यानुमते तदा) 15. 25. 12-13; (2) When Yudhiṣṭhira went to meet Dhṛta-rāṣṭra he crossed the river Yamunā and saw from a distance the आश्रम of the royal sage Śatayūpa (and that of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra) (स ददर्शाश्रमं दूराद् राजर्षेः  … शतयूपस्य) 15. 30. 17.
शरभङ्गाश्रम: Śarabhaṅgāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। A. Location: In the great forest Daṇḍa-kāraṇya 3. 261. 40. B. Holiness: One who visited the आश्रम did not experience misery and purified his family (शरभङ्गाश्र-मं गत्वा … न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नोति पुनाति च कुलं नरः) 3. 83. 39. C. Rāmāyaṇa event: Fearing the return of the citizens, Rāma entered the great forest and went to the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga; he honour-ed there Śarabhaṅga and took his residence in Daṇḍakāraṇya (प्रविवेश महार-ण्यं शरभङ्गाश्रमं प्रति । सत्कृत्य शरभङ्गं स दण्डकारण्यम् आश्रितः) 3. 261. 39-40.
शाकल: Śākala nt.: Name of a city. A. Location: To the west of Indra-prastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रती-चीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; the principal town of the Madra country (मद्राणां पुटभेदनम्) 2. 29. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 32. 14 cites Amara (2. 2. 1) पत्तनं पुटभेदनम्); in the Bāhlīka country (बाह्लीकेषूषितं मया । … शाकलं नाम नगरम्) 8. 30. 13-14. B. Description: Pro-sperous (स्फीत) 8. 30. 29; people living there called शाकलावतः 8. 30. 33. C. Characteristic: In the Śākala town a Rākṣasī beat the drum on every four-teenth day of the dark fortnight of the month and sang songs in which it was said: when would the loud singers (? घोषि-काः) sing again गाथास् in Śākala after eating beef and drinking wine of गुड ? (तत्र स्म राक्षसी गाति सदा कृष्णचतुर्-दशीम् । नगरे शाकले स्फीते आहत्य निशि दुन्दुभिम् ॥ कदा वा घोषिका गाथाः पुनर् गास्यन्ति शाकले । गव्यस्य तृप्ता मांसस्य पीत्वा गौडं महासवम् ॥ ) 8. 30. 29-30. D. Epic event: Nakula went to Śākala in his expedition before the Rājasūya and won over Śalya, his maternal uncle, by taking recourse to affection (and not battle) (ततः शाकलम् अभ्येत्य … मातुलं प्रीति-पूर्वेण शल्यं चक्रे वशे बली ॥ ) 2. 29. 13.
शालग्राम: Śālagrāma m.: Name of a village. A village sacred to Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa; Hari is always present there; by approach-ing Viṣṇu there one got the fruit of Aśva-medha sacrifice and went to the world of Viṣṇu (स्थानं नारायणस्य तु । सदा संनिहितो यत्र हरिर् वसति भारत । शाल-ग्राम इति ख्यातो विष्णोर् अद्भुतकर्मणः । अभिगम्य … विष्णुम् … । अश्वमेधम् अवा-प्नोति विष्णुलोकं च गच्छति ॥ ) 3. 82. 106-107; there is a well there which freed the visitor of all sins; four oceans are present in it; by bathing in the well one did not meet with calamity (तत्रोदपानो धर्मज्ञ सर्वपापप्रमोचनः । समुद्रास् तत्र चत्वारः कूपे संनिहिताः सदा । ततोप-स्पृश्य राजेन्द्र न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ ) 3. 82. 108.
शिव: Śiva nt.: Name of a house in Vāraṇā-vata meant for the Pāṇḍavas. A. Location: In the town Vāraṇāvata (वारणावतम् अद्यैव यथा यासि तथा कुरु ॥ तत्र गत्वा … गृहं … कारयेथाः । ।) 1. 132. 7-8 (गृहं शिवाख्यम्) 1. 134. 11; the house was constructed near the store of arms (आयुधागारम् आश्रित्य) 1. 132. 8. B. Description: Inauspicious (अशिव) 1. 134. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 146. 11: शिवम् इत्य् आख्यामात्रम् अर्थतस् त्व् अशिवं मरणा-र्थं कृतत्वात्); expensive (महाधन) 1. 132. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 144. 8: महा-धनं बहुधनसाध्यम्); it had four halls and was well enclosed (चतुःशालं गृहं परमसंवृतम्) 1. 132. 8. C. Furniture: Essential seats and beds as well as conveyances for the use of the Pāṇḍavas were provided in the house (तत्रासनानि मुख्यानि यानानि शयनानि च । विधातव्यानि पाण्डवानाम्) 1. 132. 14. D. Materials used in the construction of the house: Hemp, resin, मुञ्ज, बल्वज, bamboo; these and other materials used in its constru-ction were sprinkled with घृत; (शणसर्-जरसं व्यक्तम् आनीतं गृहकर्मणि । मुञ्जबल्वजवंशादि द्रव्यं सर्वं घृ-तोक्षितम् ॥ ) 1. 134. 14; Duryodhana had asked Purocana to use in the construction of the house hemp, resin and all such in-flammable material; the clay meant to be used as plaster of the walls was to be mixed with butter, oil, and lac in ample quantity; hemp, bamboo, घृत, and wood and other contrivances (? यन्त्राणि) of different kinds were to be used in all parts of the house; it was to be inflammable (शणसर्जरसादीनि यानि द्रव्याणि कानिचित् । आग्नेयान्य् उत सन्तीह तानि सर्वाणि दापय ॥ सर्पिषा च सतैलेन लाक्षया चाप्यनल्पया । मृत्तिकां मिश्रयि-त्वा त्वं लेपं कुड्येषु दापयेः ॥ शणान् वंशं घृतं दारु यन्त्राणि विविधानि च । तस्मिन् वेश्मनि सर्वाणि निक्षिपेथाः समन्-ततः ॥ … आग्नेयम् इति तत् कार्यम्) 1. 132. 9-12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 144. 9: आग्ने-यानि अग्निसंदीपकानि). E. Epic events: (1) Purocana led the Pāṇḍavas to this house called Śiva (पुरोचनः । निवेदयाम् आस गृहं शिवाख्यम् अशिवं तदा) 1. 134. 11; (2) When the Pāṇḍavas entered it, Yudhiṣṭhira, on smelling the odour of fat mixed with clarified butter and lac, realized that the house was highly inflammable (उवाचाग्नेयम् इत्य् एवं भीमसेनं युधि-ष्ठिरः । जिघ्रन् सोम्य वसागन्धं सर्पिर्-जतुविमिश्रितम् ॥ कृतं हि व्यक्तम् आग्नेयम् इदं वेश्म) 1. 134. 13-14, 18; (इदं शरणम् आग्नेयम्) 1. 135. 10; Purocana was always present at the entrance of the house (स तत्र च गृहद्वारि वसत्य् अशुभ-धीः सदा) 1. 135. 18; (3) A digger, sent by Vidura, dug a big tunnel in the middle of the house; its opening was not very wide; it was covered with a wooden plank, unknown to others and level with the ground; its opening was concealed lest Purocana noticed it; the Pāṇḍavas were to escape through this tunnel (खनको यत्नम् आस्थितः । परिखाम् उत्किरन् नाम चकार सुमहद् बिलम् ॥ चक्रे च वेश्म-नस् तस्य मध्ये नातिमहन् मुखम् । कपाटयुक्तम् अज्नातम् समं भूम्या च भारत ॥ पुरोचनभयाच् चैव व्यदधात् संवृतं मुखम्) 1. 135. 16-18; (4) A Niṣādī who came to the lac-house for food with her five sons, drank wine and slept in the same house 1. 136. 7-8; (5) The burning of the house was blamed on Puro-cana by the people (दुर्योधनप्रयुक्तेन पापेनाकृतबुद्धिना । गृहम् आत्मविनाशाय कारितं दाहितं च तत् ॥ ) 1. 136. 11; 1. 137. 2.

Śiva m. (pl.): Name of a certain group of Brāhmaṇas. They lived in the south; they are de-scribed as सिद्ध; they were well-versed in the Vedas; they studied the Vedas along with their supplements and then went to the abode of Yama (इयं … दक्षिणेत्य् उच्यतेऽथ दिक्) 5. 107. 1; (अत्र सिद्धाः शिवा नाम ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः । अधीत्य सखिलान् वेदान् आलभन्ते यमक्षयम् ॥ ) 5. 107. 18.
शिशुमारपुर: Śiśumārapura nt.: Name of a town. The kings, Duryodhana and others all gathered at Śiśumārapura for the स्वयं-वर of Draupadī; the sages, desirous to see the स्वयंवर, and the Brāhmaṇas from different countries reached there; then all the subjects of the king also reached there and they and the kings settled down at Śiśumārapura (ततः पौरजनाः सर्वे …  … शिशुमारपुरं प्राप्य न्यविशंस् ते च पार्थिवाः ॥ ) 1. 176. 12-15; the enclosure for the gathering was erected to the north-east of the town on an even and auspicious spot (प्रागुत्तरेण नगराद् भूमिभागे समे शुभे । समाजवाटः शुशुभे) 1. 176. 16. [See Kāmpilya, Pāñcālanagara]
शुकस्य: Śukasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of the आश्रम of the high-souled Śuka. Situated near the आश्रम of Śarabhaṅga; by visiting it one did not meet with misery and he purified his family (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नोति पुनाति च कुलं नरः) 3. 83. 39.
शृङ्गवेरपुर: Śṛṅgaverapura nt.: Name of a town. Near Gaṅgā 3. 83. 63; described as big (महन्त्) 3. 83. 62; it was at Śṛigavera-pura that Rāma crossed the river (Gaṅgā) (यत्र तीर्णो महाराज रामो दाश्रथिः पुरा) 3. 83. 62.
शैरीषक: Śairīṣaka nt.: Name of a town ? To the west of Indraprastha (निर्याय प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; described as fertile (बहुधान्यक) 2. 29. 5; Nakula in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya subjugated it (शैरिषकं … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 6.
श्यामाया: Śyāmāyā āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। Mentioned in the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama 13. 26. 3; by visit-ing the आश्रम of Śyāmā and by living and bathing there for nine nights at a stretch one would live in the Gandharvanagara (उष्य चैवाभिषिच्य च । त्रींस् त्रिरात्रान् स सं-धाय गन्धर्वनगरे वसेत् ॥ ) 13. 26. 28.
श्रावस्ती: Śrāvastī f.: Name of a city. It was founded by king, Śrāvasta(ka) of the Ikṣvāku family (जज्ञे श्रावस्तको राजा श्रावस्ती येन निर्मिता) 3. 193. 4.
श्वेतकेतोर्: *Śvetaketor āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम where Śvetaketu lived. Described as holy (पुण्य) and where the trees always gave fruit (सदाफलैर् उपपन्नं महीजैः) 3. 132. 1; Śvetaketu lived there with his father Uddālaka, his sister Sujātā who was married to Kahoḍa, and Kahoḍa's son Aṣṭāvakra 3. 132. 3 ff; in the आश्रम Śvetaketu saw Sarasvatī in human form; he said to her, who had appeared there, that he would like to know from her the (nature of) ‘speech’. (साक्षाद् अत्र श्वेतकेतुर् ददर्श सरस्वतीं मानुषरूपदेहाम् । वेत्स्यामि वाणीम् इति संप्रवृत्तां सरस्वतीं श्वेतकेतुर् ब-भाषे) 3. 132. 2.
शक: Śaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10 37, 5; (वक्रभयाः शकाः) 6. 10. 43; listed by him again along with Niṣādas and Niṣadhas (शका निषादा निषधास् … ) 6. 10. 50. B. Origin: They were produced, along with Śabaras, by Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha's cow, from her dung (शकृतः शबराञ् शकान्) 1. 165. 35; elsewhere it is stated that they were originally Kṣatriyas but were degraded to the status of a वृषल due to their neglect of Brāhmaṇas (क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 33. 19. C. Description and characteristics: Very strong (अतिबल) 8. 5. 18, (बलिन्) 8. 51. 19; very frightful (सुघोर), having frightful eyes (घोरचक्षुस्) 7. 68. 41; rough, doers of cruel deeds (उग्र, क्रूर-कर्मन्) 8. 51. 18; impure (अशुचि), having shaven, half-shaven heads, or having mat-ted hair on heads and with bearded faces (मुण्डार्धमुण्डजटिलान् … जटिलाननान्) 7. 68. 44; they knew the मायास् of demons (विदन्त्य् असुरमायां ये) 7. 68. 41; excit-ed, fond of wars, firm-fisted (संरंभिन्, युद्धशौण्ड, दृब्धपाणि) 8. 51. 19; quick in action (लघुहस्त) 7. 95. 32; difficult to be conquered (दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18; difficult to be assailed (दुराधर्ष), fiery, shining like burning fire (अग्निकल्प) (प्रदीप्तैर् इव पावकैः); their valour was like that of Indra (शक्रतुल्यपराक्रम) 7. 87. 50; characterized as म्लेच्छस् 7. 68. 44; 7. 95. 13; they lived in the caves of mountains (गिरिगह्वरवासिन्) 7. 68 45; also said to be living on country-side but leading the life of Dasyus (सर्वे विषय-वासिनः … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15; D. Epic events: (1) Śakas were among several peoples like Cīnas, Hūṇas and others who, although they brought tribute of different kinds for Rājasūya, were stopped at the gate (अभिगतान् विविधान् द्वारि वारितान्; बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 19-20, 25; the details of their tribute given in 2. 47. 21-25; Śakas are mentioned once again along with Tukhāras and others who brought tribute in the form of an अर्बुद horses who could go long distances and were of noble descent, as well as gold in very large quan-tities to be counted by crores and totalling a पद्म, but were stopped at the gate (महागमान् दूरगमान् गणितान् अर्बुदं हयान् ॥ कोटिशश् चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्मसंमितम् ॥ बलिम् आदाय विविधं द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 47. 26-27; they are mentioned a third time along with Aṅgas, Vaṅgas and others whose kings (क्षत्रियाः) brought large amount of wealth as tribute (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शत-शः); when asked by the gate-keepers to give more, each one of them gave a thou-sand elephants from the Kāmyaka lake and then were allowed to enter; the elephants given by them are described in stanzas 2. 48. 15-20; Kṛṣṇa mentioned Śakas among those whose kings, afraid of the lustre of the weapons of Pāṇḍavas, acted as servers at the Rājasūya sacrifice (शकान् । … मही-पालान् शस्त्रतेजोभयार्दितान् । … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 20, 22; (2) Drupada asked Yudhiṣṭhira to send his messengers to the kings of Śakas and others to seek their help in war 5. 4. 7, 9, 15; (3) Kāmboja Sudakṣiṇa came to Duryodhana with an army of अक्षौहिणी fighters consi-sting of Yavanas and Śakas; it looked like a swarm of locusts (तस्य सेनासमावायः शलभानाम् इवाबभौ) 5. 19. 21-22; Duryodhana's army consisted of different peoples, Śakas being one of them; like the army of gods it was difficult to be attacked (दुराधर्षां देवचमूप्रकाशाम्) 5. 158. 19-20; Śaka kings with their armies led by Śakuni marched towards Kurukṣetra in the second division of the Kaurava army (शकाः … द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 7; there, on the battle-field, before the start of the war, Kṛpa along with Śakas, Kirātas and others protected the Kaurava army in the north (चमूम् उत्तरतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 13; (4) On the third day of the war, the Kāmboja king along with the Śakas was posted at the ‘tail’ (पुच्छम् आसन्) of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2) of Kauravas 6. 52. 7; (5) On the sixth day, Śakas, Yavanas and others stood at the right wing (दक्षिणम् पक्षम् आश्रित्य) of the Krauñca-vyūha (6. 71. 14) of the Kauravas 6. 71. 20; (6) On the eleventh day, Śakas, Yavanas and others riding swift horses stood at the extreme end of the left wing (सव्यं पार्श्वं … तेषां प्रपक्षाः … ययुर् अश्वैर् महावेगैः) of the Śakaṭavyūha (7. 6. 15) of Kauravas 7. 6. 4-5; (7) On the eleventh day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, while recounting past exploits of Kṛṣṇa remembered his victory over hordes of enemies consisting of Āvan-tyas and others who came from different directions and joined the Śakas riding horses (?) (आवन्त्यान् … नानादिग्भ्यश् च संप्राप्तान् व्रातान् अश्वशकान् प्रति । जितवान् पुण्डरीकाक्षो … ) 7. 10. 16-18 (See Editor's note on the stanza Vol. IX. pp. 1144-1145: श्ब्र्। (शतपथ ब्राह्मण) appears to use this word to signify ‘excrement of a horse’! Here it seems to mean a particular (disgusting ?) tribe of Śakas who were horse-riders (cf. {#aSvapuruza#} in 6. 1. 7); (8) On the twelfth day, Śakas were among those who occupied the ‘neck’ (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4) of Kaura-vas 7. 19. 7-8; (9) On the fourteenth day, fierce Śakas, Yavanas and others formed innumerable hordes in hundreds and thousands (व्राताः शतसहस्रशः) to attack Arjuna; he fought them with arrows and cut them off with his skill in shooting arrows (अशातयत् … अस्त्रमायया); afraid, they all fled 7. 68. 41-45; (10) The same day, Sātyaki expected to encounter them in his onward march towards Arjuna (शकैश् चापि समेष्यामि) 7. 87. 50; Sātyaki asked his charioteer to drive his chariot to Śakas and other Mlecchas who, riding chariots and elephants and holding different kinds of weapons in their hands, were eager to fight with him (माम् एवाभिमुखाः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति समरार्थिनः); Sātyaki was con-fident to defeat them 7. 95. 13-14; in the encounter that followed, Śakas and others showered arrows on Sātyaki; he cut off their arrows and killed them by thousands covering the earth with their blood and flesh; those who escaped death fled swiftly in fright; Sātyaki thus defeated the large army of Śakas 7. 95. 32-33, 38-39, 45; three thousand horse-riders of Śakas and others, led by Duryodhana, returned to the battlefield to attack Sātyaki; he killed many of them 7. 97. 13-14, 20; (11) On the seventeenth day, Kāmbojas, Śakas and Yavanas, led by Saṃśaptakas guarded the extremity of the left side (वामं पार्श्वम् अपालयन् … तेषां प्रपक्षः) of the Bārha-spatyavyūha (8. 31. 26) of Kauravas 8. 31. 14-15; in the course of that day, after the death of the younger brother of Kāmboja Sudakṣiṇa, there was fierce fighting (घोरम् अद्भुतदर्शनम्) in which Śakas riding horses took part; a large number of them were killed 8. 40. 107-110; later that day, Kṛṣṇa in order to encourage Arjuna told him that Śakas had joined the Kaurava army for the sake of Duryodhana and no one else but he (Arjuna) could defeat them (न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप) 8. 51. 18, 20; Śakas, who held excellent weapons in their hands and were ready to shoot arrows, riding horses, chariots and elephants, rushed at Arjuna to kill him (आततायिनः । शकास् … ॥ वरायुधान् पाणिग-तान्); Arjuna cut off their hands and heads, killed their horses and elephants and broke their chariots 8. 64. 16-17; (12) On the seventeenth day, at night (निशि 8. 1. 25), when Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the death of Karṇa, he while remembering the past heroism of Karṇa mentioned that he had formerly defeated Śakas and many others and made them pay tribute (चक्रे बलिभृ-तः पुरा) 8. 5. 18, 20 (reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय at the time of Duryodhana's वैष्णवयज्ञ 3. 241. 19, 32 (Vol. 4. App. I. 24. 28-34); (13) On the eighteenth day, Kṛpa with Śakas and Yavanas stood on the right side (दक्षिणे पार्श्वे) of the Sarvatobhadravyūha (9. 7. 19) of Kaura-vas 9. 7. 24; (14) At the end of the war, Saṃjaya mentioned Śakas among those who were killed in the war 9. 1. 26; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra remembered that Śakas and others had joined his side not caring for death while fighting (मदर्थम् उद्यताः सर्वे प्राणांस् त्यक्त्वा रणे); Duryodhana boast-ed his ability to fight with Pāṇḍavas due to the support of Śakas 9. 2. 8, 21-22. E. Past event: Māndhātṛ once asked Indra how people like Śakas were to be made to follow Dharma and how kings like him should control them (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते  … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः); Indra thereupon told Māndhātṛ the duties of Dasyus (the term Dasyu apparently covered Śakas) 12. 65. 13, 15, 17-21. F. Future event: Śakas are mentioned among many kings who at the end of the Yuga (यु-गान्ते समनुप्राप्ते) 3. 186. 30; युगान्ते 3. 186. 33; युगक्षये 3. 186. 43, 48) would rule the earth the wrong way, would be sinful and would be given to tell lies (मि-थ्यानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः) 3. 186. 29-30.
शण्ड: Śaṇḍa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda told a certain king that Śaṇḍas were the bodily dirt of Mauṣṭikas and those whose sacrificial priests were of the warrior caste were the dirt of Śaṇḍas (मौष्टिकानां मलं शण्डाः शण्डानां राजयाजकाः) 8. 30. 70.
शबर: Śabara m. (pl.): Name of a forest tribe. A. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; अटवी शबराश् चैव 6. 10. 46 (Are Aṭavī-śabaras living in the north different from the other Śabaras who lived in the south ? see the next); (2) Śabaras who lived in the south (दक्षिणापथजन्मानः) 12. 200. 39 (these are, however, not listed by Saṃ-jaya among the southern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 56-63ab). B. Origin: (1) Angered Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, created Śabaras from her dung (असृजत् … शकृतः शबरान् … क्रोधमूर्च्छिता) 1. 165. 35; this event is said to have occurred also on a different occasion; when Viśvā-mitra's army destroyed the forest near Vasi-ṣṭha's आश्रम, he angered, asked his cow to produce Śabaras; accordingly she pro-duced them (क्रुद्धो … वसिष्ठः … । सृजस्व शबरान् घोरान् इति स्वां गाम् उवाच ह) 9. 39. 20; (2) Some Kṣatriyas are also said to have been degraded to the state of a वृषल due to their disregard of Brāhmaṇas (शबरबर्बराः ॥ … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ ) 13. 35. 17-18; elsewhere it is stated that the Kṣatriyas who killed Jamadagni became वृषल due to their transgressing the धर्म of Kṣa-triyas and their disregard of Brāhmaṇas (तेषां (i. e. क्षत्रियाणाम्) … प्रजा वृषल-तां प्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ त एते … पुण्ड्राश् च शबरैः सह । वृषलत्वं परिगता व्युत्थानात् क्षत्रधर्मतः ॥ ) 14. 29. 15-16; (3) But at one place it is mentioned that Śabaras and others existed since the Tretāyuga (त्रेताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना … (i. e. Śabaras and others) 12. 200. 39, 42. C. Description: Fierce, fierce to look at (घोर, घोरदर्शन) 9. 39. 20-21. D. Their low status: They are characterized as दस्युस् 12. 65. 17, 21; also cf. F. Past events (2) below; those men who did not perform sacrifices remained for ever in the nether worlds and did not go to heaven; such men are compared with Pulindas and Śabaras (अर्वाक् च प्रति-तिष्ठन्ति पुलीन्दशबरा इव । न ह्य् अयज्ञा अमुं लोकं प्राप्नुवन्ति कथंचन) 12. 147. 8; they are included among those people who, though they lived in countries, led the life of दस्युस् (शबरबर्बराः । … सर्वे विषयवासिनः । सर्वे ते दस्युजीवि-नः ॥ ) 12. 65. 13, 15; they did not believe in Bhūtapati as the अध्यक्ष (of the world); sinful, they roamed over the earth leading the life of dogs, crows, बलस् (?) and vultures (निरध्यक्षांस् तु कौन्तेय कीर्त-यिष्यामि … । उत्साः पुलिन्दाः शबरा … ॥ एते पापकृतस् तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । श्वकाकबलगृध्राणां सधर्माणो … ॥ ) 12. 200. 38-39, 41. E. Epic events: (1) On the second day of the war, Śabaras on the side of Pāṇḍavas stood on the left side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of Pāṇḍavas (वामं पार्श्वं समाश्रिताः) 6. 46. 51; (2) On the fourteenth day, Sātyaki killed thousands of Śabaras (on the side of Kauravas); he covered the ground with their flesh and blood, and also with their shaven heads and head gears (सशिर-स्त्राणैः शिरोभिर् लूनमूर्धजैः) 7. 95. 38-40. F. Past event: (1) King Mān-dhātṛ once asked Indra the nature of the धर्म of people like Śabaras and how kings like him should govern them (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः) 12. 65. 13-15; thereupon Indra told him the duties of Dasyus (the term apparently covers Śabaras) 12. 65. 17-21; (2) A certain Brāhmaṇa, Gau-tama by name, took residence in the house of a Dasyu which is later designated as the excellent house (गृहवर) of a rich, Śabara (शबरालय) 12. 162. 30, 34; 12. 165. 5; 12. 167. 16 (see Dasyu, Past events I, no. 7, p. 750 above).
शरदण्ड: Śaradaṇḍa m. (pl. ?): Name of a country. The horses of this country were referred to as शरदण्डज; these horses were yoked to the chariot of Daṇḍaketu (शरदण्डानु-दण्डजाः । … दण्डकेतुम् उदावहन्) 7. 22. 58 [See Editor's note on the stanza, Cr. Edn. Vol. 9, pp. 1147-1148: “ … Śaradaṇḍa and Anudaṇḍa would be names of different countries. We know nothing of Anudaṇḍa, but Śaradaṇḍa was the name of a country belonging to Śālva in Madhyadeśa (Kāśikā on Pāṇini IV. 1. 173: शरदण्डाश् च शाल्वा-वयवसंज्ञिताः)”].
शर्मक: Śarmaka m. (pl.): Name of a people.
शर्मिल: Śarmila m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of war, Duryodhana along with Śarmilas and others gave pro-tection to the army of Śakuni (शर्मिल-कोसलैः ॥ … अभ्यरक्षत … सौबलेयस्य वाहिनीम्) 6. 47. 15-16.
शाकद्वीप: Śākadvīpa nt. (sg.): Name of one of the seven Dvīpas. A. Location and extent: According to Draupadī, it was similar to Krauñca-dvīpa and lay to the east of Mahāmeru; the Dvīpa known as Bhadrāśva which lay to the north of Mahāmeru was in extent equal to Śākadvīpa (क्रौञ्चद्वीपेन स-दृशः शाकद्वीपो … । पूर्वेण तु महा-मेरोः … उत्तरेण महामेरोः शाकद्वीपेन संमितः । भद्राश्वः … ॥ ) 12. 14 23-24; according to Saṃjaya, Śākadvīpa was double the size of Jambūdvīpa and the ocean which surrounded it was also double its size (जम्बूद्वीपप्रमाणेन द्विगुणः स … । विष्कम्भेण महाराज सागरोऽपि विभागशः । क्षीरोदो भरतश्रेष्ठ येन संपरिवारितः) 6. 12. 9; Śākadvīpa was larger than Jambūdvīpa both in length and breadth (परिवार्य तु कौरव्य दैर्-घ्यं ह्रस्वत्वम् एव च । जम्बूद्वीपेन) 6. 12. 25. B. Some geographical details of the Śākadvīpa: There are seven mountains on Śākadvīpa (Meru, Malaya, Jaladhāra, Raivataka, Śyāma, Durgaśaila and Kesarī); the mountains are described in 6. 12. 13-21 (for which see Vol. I, section 5); the Varṣas related to these mountains are detailed in 6. 12. 22-24. C. Possible explanation of the name: A famous big tree named Śāka stood in its middle (that was why probably the Dvīpa was so called) ( … विख्यातस् तस्य मध्ये महा-द्रुमः ॥ शाको नाम महाराज तस्य द्वीपस्य मध्यगः । ) 6. 12. 25-26. D. Description of the countries and the peoples of Śākadvīpa: Highly lustrous (महौजस्) 6. 12. 37; the Janapadas on this Dvipa were holy; famine was not known; the people were endowed with for-bearance and lustre; they did not die (तत्र पुण्या जनपदा (also 6. 12. 33) न तत्र म्रियते जनः । कुत एव हि दुर्भिक्षं क्षमातेजोयुता हि ते ॥ ) 6. 12. 10; God Śaṅkara was worshipped there (पूज्यते तत्र शंकरः); Siddhas, Cāraṇas and various deities visited it (तत्र गच्छन्ति सिद्धाश् च चारणा दैवतानि च) 6. 12 26-27; all the four kinds of subjects were highly religious (धार्मिकाश् च प्रजा … चत्वारो ऽतीव … ) 6. 12. 27; the Varṇas followed their respective duties; they were long-lived, free from oldage and death; they multiplied like the rivers in the rainy season (प्रजास् तत्र विवर्धन्ते वर्षास्व् इव समुद्रगाः) 6. 12. 28-29; no thief was ever met with there (न च स्तेनोऽत्र दृश्यते) 6. 12. 28; there was no king, no punishment, nor the officers to inflict punishment (न तत्र राजा राजेन्द्र न दण्डो न च दण्डिकाः); by following their respective धर्मस् the people pro-tected it and also protected one another (स्वधर्मेणैव धर्मं च ते रक्षन्ति परस्परम्) 6. 12. 36; the four holy Jana-padas on the Dvīpa, honoured in the worlds (लोकसंमताः), are known as Maga, Maśaka, Mānasa and Mandaga; they are described 6, 12. 33-36; the holy rivers on the Śākadvīpa are Gaṅgā, flowing in various streams (बहुधागतिः), Sukumārī, Kumārī, Sītā, Kāverakā, Mahānadī, Maṇi-jalā, and Ikṣuvardhanikā; several hundreds and thousands of holy rivers arose from them, from the waters of which Indra gave rain (यतो वर्षति वासवः); it is not possible to name them all nor to describe their extent; all these excellent rivers are holy (न तासां नामधेयानि परिमाणं तथैव च । शक्यते परिसंख्यातुं पुण्यास् ता हि सरिद्वराः) 6. 12. 29-32. E. Epic events: (1) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the Śāka-dvīpa; Saṃjaya agreed and described it in brief (शाकद्वीपस्य संक्षेपो … ) 6. 12. 2, 11; on Dhṛtarāṣṭra's further request to describe the Dvīpa in details (विस्तरम्) Saṃjaya described it in some detail which was worth hearing (एतावद् एव श्रोतव्यम्); that was about all that Saṃjaya could tell about the Dvīpa 6. 12. 12, 37; (2) In order to revive the spirits of Yudhiṣṭhira after the war, Draupadī reminded him that formerly he had passed through the ocean and brought under control various large Dvīpas including the Śākadvīpa and the islands in-between and the Janapadas situated on them (शाकद्वीपो … । … दण्डेन मृदितस् त्वया; द्वीपाश् च सान्तरद्वीपा नानाजनपदालयाः । विगाह्य सागरं वीर दण्डेन मृदितास् त्वया) 12. 14. 23, 25 (a reference to Arjuna's expedition before the Rājasūya 2. 23. 15-16; Nīlakaṇṭha on Bom. Ed. 12. 14. 23: क्रौञ्चद्वीपादिवशीकरणम् सिद्धद्वारा (?) राजसूये).
शाकलावत्: Śākalāvat m. (pl.): People living in the town Śākala. Karṇa while deriding Śalya told him what a certain Brāhmaṇa had once told Dhṛtarāṣṭra (8. 30. 7, 28); according to him the people of the town Śākala, young and old, well-adorned, and their fair and large women, ate meat of many rams mixed with onions and गण्डूष (?), as also meat of pigs, fowls, cows, asses and camels; they said that the lives of those who did not eat meat of sheep was futile; they danced and sang songs of this nature when they drank liquor; good conduct was not expected of such people (ऐडं च ये न खादन्ति तेषां जन्म निरर्थ-कम् ॥ इति गायन्ति ये मत्ताः शीधुना शाकलावतः । सबालवृद्धाः कूर्दन्तस् तेषु वृत्तं कथं भवेत् ॥ ) 8. 30. 31-33; also cf. Śākala city p. 573).
शानवत्य: Śānavatya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (शानवत्या गयास् तथा । … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशोऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 15-16; they and others were stopped at the gate by gate-keepers and were asked to give more to get entrance (कृतकाराः सुबलयस् ततो द्वारम् अवाप्स्यथ); when each one of them then gave one thousand elephants from the Kāmyaka forest they were allowed to enter (अभितः काम्यकं सरः । दत्त्वैकैको दशशतान् कुञ्जरान्) 2. 48. 18-20; the elephants described in 2. 48. 19-20.
शाल्व: Śālva, Śālveya, Śālveyaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; people once referred to as शाल्वाश्रयाः 6. 114. 77. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas of Bhārata-varṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शाल्वमाद्रेयजाङ्गलाः) 6. 10. 37; designated as Janapada also in 4. 1. 9; 6. 18. 13-14; 6. 114. 77, and as Rāṣṭra in 4. 1. 8; the Janapada lay around Kurus (परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 9. B. Description: (1) Of the Janapada: pleasant (रम-णीय), (रम्य) 4. 1. 8-9; rich in food (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; well-protected (गुप्त) 4. 1. 8; (2) Of the warriors: brave (शूर) and prepared to die while fighting (तनुत्यज्) 6. 18. 14. C. Epic events: (1) Śālvas were among those peoples who, afraid of Jarāsandha, had left north to take shelter in the south; their (of Śālveyas) kings also, along with their brothers and followers, fled to the south (शाल्वाः पट-च्चराः । … शाल्वेयानां च राजानः सोदर्या-नुचरैः सह … तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परित्यज्य भयार्दिताः … दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः) 2. 13. 25-27; (2) Jayadratha, wanting to marry, was proceeding to the country of Śālveyas (शाल्वेयान् प्रयातः सो ऽभवत् तदा) 3. 248. 6; (3) Śālva was one of the countries recommended by Arjuna to Yudhiṣṭhira for their stay during the year of अज्ञातवास 4. 1. 8-10; (4) Śālveyakas, along with Matsyas led by Kīcaka, had often subdued Suśarman, the king of Tri-gartas (अस्कृन् निकृतः पूर्वं मत्स्यैः शाल्वेयकैः सह) 4. 29. 2; (5) Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Śālveyas were among those who did not respect him any longer and had gone to the side of Pāṇḍa-vas (शाल्वेयाः … सर्वे त्वाम् अवजानते) 5. 53. 17; (6) According to Saṃjaya's report, the five Kekaya brothers (on the side of Pāṇḍavas) were supposed to engage the Śālvas and Kekayas (both, on the side of Kauravas) in the forthcoming war (राजपुत्रा भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः । … योत्स्यन्ति संयुगे ॥ तेषाम् एव कृतो भागो  … शाल्वकेकयाः । ) 5. 56. 17-18; (7) Ulūka informed Yudhiṣṭhira that Duryodhana's army, which included Śālvas and others and was protected by their kings, had be-come unassailable and had become like the army of the gods (दुराधर्षां देवचमू-प्रकाशां) 5. 158. 19-20; (8) Bhīṣma had assured Duryodhana that he alone would kill the Pāṇḍava army along with Śālve-yakas; that was his responsibility (अहं हन्ता पाण्डवानाम् अनीकं शाल्वेयकांश् चेति ममैष भारः) 5. 160. 10; (9) On the battle-field before the start of the war, Śālvas were among the twelve Janapadas, whose twenty thousand chariot-fighters (रथा विंशतिसाहस्राः), offered protection to Bhīṣma (द्वादशैते जनपदाः … महता रथवंशेन तेऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम्) 6. 18. 12-14; (10) On the first day of the war, Śālvas led by Jayadratha and other heroes, were stationed in the middle of the army (शाल्वा मत्स्याः … सर्वसैन्यस्य मध्ये) 6. 20. 12; (11) On the fifth day, Sātyaki, Cekitāna and Abhimanyu attacked Śālvas and Kekayas 6. 68. 8; (12) On the tenth day, the chariot-fighters (महारथाः) of Śālvas and others, insti-gated by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102-106), attacked Arjuna; Arjuna burnt them with heavenly missiles (दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राणि सं-चिन्त्य … ददाह); afflicted by Arjuna's arrows and their chariots and banners broken (विप्रकीर्णरथध्वजाः), they did not attack Arjuna (नाभ्यवर्तन्त … वानर-ध्वजम्); he scattered their army (द्राव-यित्वा वरूथिनीम्) (6. 112. 110-117); later, the same day, just before the fall of Bhīṣma, Śālvas were among the twelve Janapadas who, though they were afflicted by arrows and pained due to wounds (शरार्ता व्रण-पीडिताः) did not abandon Bhīṣma fighting with Arjuna, even when the Kaurava army fled due to fear (वयं … भीताः … प्रद्रवाम महारणात्; … शाल्वाश्रयास् … द्वादशैते जनपदाः शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मं युध्यमानं किरीटिना) 6. 114. 75-77; (13) On the fourteenth day, Matsyas along with the armies of Śālveyas, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Virāṭa, speedily attacked Droṇa (मत्-स्याः शाल्वेयसेनाश् च द्रोणम् आजग्मुर् अञ्जसा) 7. 73. 50; in the evening of that day (सायाह्ने 7. 129. 5), they again attacked Droṇa 7. 129. 7; (14) On the sixteenth day, Śālvas were among those who attacked Arjuna showering him with arrows; although they were getting killed, they did not leave Arjuna as the moths the fire (समरे नाजहुः पाण्डवं तदा । … शलभा इव पावकम्) 8. 19. 2-3, 7; (15) On the seventeenth day, Karṇa told Śalya what a certain Brāhmaṇa had once told Dhṛtarāṣṭra; according to him, Śālvas knew what the eternal धर्म was (धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्); he told Śalya that Śālvas knew what the speaker intend-ed to convey only when all details were told to them (अर्धोक्ताः कुरुपाञ्चालाः शाल्वाः कृत्स्नानुशासिनः) 8. 30. 8, 60-61, 79. F. Past event: (1) King Dyumat-sena once ruled the Śālvas until he became blind 3. 278. 7; after some years his subjects approached him in the forest to request him to rule over them once again (ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वाः शाल्वेभ्यो ऽभ्या-गता … ) 3. 283. 3, 5. G. Several kings referred to as king of Śālvas (or Śālveyas): A. King of Śālvas: (a) शाल्वपति: (1) King of Śālvas (whom Ambā had first chosen as her husband) not named 5. 171. 6; 5. 172. 2, 4, 10, 14. 18; 5. 174. 3; 5. 175. 22; 5. 176. 34; (2) Śālva, the king of Saubha (the city flying in the sky) 3. 17. 8; (b) शाल्वराज: (1) Śālva, the king of Saubha (1. 96. 48), 1. 96. 25, 27, 32; 3. 17. 9, 10; 3. 18. 18; 3. 20. 22; 3. 21. 6, 8; 3. 23. 2, 27; 5. 47. 73; (2) King of Śālvas (whom Ambā had first chosen as her hus-band) 5. 171. 9; 5. 173. 6; 5. 176. 7, 11, 35; (3) A certain king (named Ugra-karman ? Maheṣvāsa ?) fighting from the side of Kauravas (उग्रकर्मा महेष्वासो नामतः कर्मतस् तथा) 8. 4. 40; (4) Dyutimant, a king of the past, who gave away his kingdom to Ṛcīka 12. 226. 33; (c) शाल्वराजन्: Śālva, the king of Saubha 1. 96. 37, 38; (d) शाल्वक: certain kings who had joined the Kaurava army, not specified 5. 30. 23; B. King of Śālveyas: शाल्वेयानाम् अधिप-; Virāṭa 5. 22. 18.
शिनि: Śini, Śaineya m. (pl.): Name of a people (descendants of Śini), a section of the Yādavas. A. Characteristic: Śaineyas, as well as Andhakas and others, by following the coun-sel of Kṛṣṇa, had tamed their enemies and delighted their friends (शैनेया हि चैत्रकाश् चान्धकाश् च … उपासीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्-धिं निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदो नन्दयन्ति ॥ ) 5. 28. 11. B. Epic event: Śaineyas, along with Andhakas and others, as dict-ated by Kāla, killed one another while fighting among themselves with pestles; the एरका blade of grass which they held in hand turned into a pestle appearing like वज्र (ततो ऽन्धकाश् च … शैनेया … । जघ्नुर् अन्योन्यम् आक्रन्दे मुसलैः कालचोदिताः ॥ ; यस् तेषाम् एरकां कश्चिद् जग्राह … । वज्र-भूतेव सा राजन्न् अदृश्यत … ॥ तृणं च मुसलीभूतम् अपि तत्र व्यदृश्यत । ) 16. 4. 36-38. C. Sātyaki is variously desig-nated with reference to Śinis or Śaineyas: A. King of Śinis: शिनीनाम् अधिप- 5. 47. 41; B. The chief (ऋषभ, पुंगव, वृषभ) of Śinis: (a) शिनीनाम् ऋष्भ-7. 89. 30; 7 115. 3; 8. 60. 23; (b) शिनि-पुंगव 5. 154. 10; 6. 54. 22; 6. 107. 3; 7. 60. 27; 7. 72. 32; 7. 85. 40, 42, 97; 7. 86. 2; 7. 87. 1; 7. 92. 43; 7. 93. 7; 7. 94. 3, 8; 7. 96. 13, 30, 35; 7. 97. 35; 7. 115. 14; 7. 116. 33; 7. 117. 2, 23; 7. 137. 30; 7. 147. 11; 7. 157. 36; 7. 164. 24, 28, 153; 7. 169. 46, 52; 8. 31. 34; 9. 16. 73; 9. 20. 9, 13, 18, 21, 23, 28; 9. 26. 3; (c) शिनिवृषभ 8. 21. 10-11; C. Delighter of Śaineyas: शैनेयनन्दन 7. 102. 16; D. Excellent of Śinis or the excellent chariot-fighter of Śinis: (a) शिनिप्रवर 7. 99. 8; (b) शिनी-नां प्रवर-रथ। 7. 89. 39; E. Excellent warrior of Śinis: शिनिप्रवीर 3. 120. 27; 5. 2. 13; 6. 55. 77-78, 82; 6. 59. 24; 7. 94. 1, 14; 7. 115. 9; 8. 21. 9; 8. 60. 6, 26; 9. 19. 25; 14. 51. 56.
शिबि: Śibi, (Śaibya) m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada (6. 18. 14; 6. 114. 77) and its people. A. Location: To the west of Khā-ṇḍavaprastha (see Epic event No. 1. below). B. Description: Brave (शूर), ready to die in battle (तनुत्यज्,) 6. 18. 14; honoured by brave (शूरसंमत) 7. 66. 39; noble (आर्य) 7. 68. 3; excellent chariot-fighters (रथोदार) 8. 4. 37 (Nī., however, in a different context, on Bom. Ed. 5. 165. 19; रथोदारः रथेष्व् एव उदारो न तु महा-रथः). C. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedition before the Rājasūya went to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha or Indra-prastha (खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 19) and subjugated Śibis 2. 29. 6; their Kṣatriyas (राजन्याः, क्षत्रियाः) brought tribute in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (आहार्षुः  … वित्तं … शतशो … ) 2. 48. 13, 16); (2) At the time of Jayadratha's attempt to abduct Draupadī, his army, consist-ing of Śibis and others, was dejected when it saw Pāṇḍavas facing them; in the battle that followed, Arjuna killed Śibi and other chiefs who came within the range of his arrows (शिबिसिन्धुत्रिगर्तानां विषादश् चाप्य् अजायत; शिबिन् … जघान … बाणगोचरम् आगतान्) 3. 255. 3, 28; (3) Led by Bhīṣma and Aśvatthāman, Śibis left Hāstinapura for Kurukṣetra in the second division of the army (द्वितीये निर्-ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 8; (4) Before the start of the war, Śibis were among the twelve Janapadas in the army of Kauravas who in a large number of chariots guarded the rear of Bhīṣma (पृष्ठगोपास् तु भी-ष्मस्य … द्वादशैते जनपदाः … महता रथवंशेन तेऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम् ॥ ) 6. 18. 10, 12, 14; (5) On the second day of war, Śibis and others protected Droṇa in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (6. 47. 10, 14); (6) On the ninth day, Śibis and others, though they were hit by sharp arrows, did not abandon Bhīṣma; on the other hand, they attacked Pāṇḍavas (सं-ग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः । … पाण्डवान् अभ्यवर्तन्त) 6. 102. 7-8; (7) On the tenth day, Śibis and others, incited by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102-107), attacked Arjuna; he burnt them with his divine weapons (दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राणि संचिन्त्य) and covered the earth with their bodies as they fell down from their chariots or from their horses and elephants; those who survived fled 6. 112. 109-117; the same day, when the Kaurava army was running away, Śibis and other eleven Janapadas did not abandon Bhīṣma though they were struck with arrows and were pained due to wounds (द्वादशैते जनपदा शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मम्) 6. 114. 76-77; (8) On the eleventh day, Śibis were among those who led by Kṛpa and others protected the ex-tremity (प्रपक्ष) of the left side (सव्यं पार्श्वम् अपालयन्) of the Śakaṭavyūha of Kauravas 7. 6. 4-6, 15; (9) On the fourteenth day, Śibis and others making a total of ten thousand chariot-fighters help-ed Jaya and Kṛtavarman who tried to check Arjuna proceeding towards Jaya-dratha; they were willing to give up their lives while fighting with Arjuna (त्यक्ता-त्मानो ऽर्जुनं प्रति); as a result, a fierce battle was fought 7. 66. 34-42; the battle is described in 7. 67. 1-5; when Sudakṣiṇa and Śrutāyudha were killed, angered Śibis and others showered arrows on Arjuna; Arjuna killed sixty hundred of them (षष्टिशतान् आर्यान्); afraid, they ran away; however, they returned only to get killed by Arjuna 7. 68. 2-6; after the death of Jayadratha, dejected Duryodhana told Droṇa that since Śibis and others were killed he would like to retire from battle and give up his life 7. 125. 31-32; Saṃjaya, in this context, mentioned Karṇa's former victory over Śibis and others (कर्णेन विजिताः पूर्वं संग्रामे) 7. 66. 39 (a reference by Saṃjaya to Karṇa's conquest of different peoples before the Vaiṣṇava-yajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 32 and Vol. IV (Āraṇyakaparvan Part 2) App. I. 24, pp. 1078-79; (10) In the night war, Yudhiṣṭhira killed many Śibis in spite of Droṇa and Kauravas 7. 132. 22-23; 7. 136. 3; Karṇa, on hearing the sound of Arjuna's bow, guessed that he must have killed all Śibis (एष सर्वाञ् शिबीन् हत्वा) 7. 145. 46; (11) On the fifteenth day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna scattered away (व्यध-मत्) Śibis and others who fought to protect Droṇa 7. 165. 24; (12) On the sixteenth day, Trigartas along with Śibis and many others attacked Arjuna and showered numerous arrows on him; though they were being destroyed by Arjuna, they did not give up fighting with him 8. 19. 2, 5-7; (13) On the seventeenth day, after the death of Karṇa, Saṃjaya return-ed to Hāstinapura at night (निशि 8. 1. 25) and while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra named Śibis among those who were killed in war 8. 4. 37. C. Past event: King Uśīnara of Śibis offered the hawk (Indra) the prosperous kingdom of Śibis in lieu of the dove (Agni) (राज्यं शिबीनाम् ऋद्धं … ) 3. 131. 20. D. Certain persons referred to with words expressive of their relation-ship with king Śibi or Śibi people: A. Son of Śibi: (i) शिबिपुत्र: Gopati 12. 49. 70; (ii) शिबिसूनु: Vṛṣādarbhi 13. 94. 8; (also see शैब्य C below); B. Pro-minent among Śibis: शिबीनां प्रवर-; Koṭikāśya (also see शैब्य C below); C. Related to Śibis: (i) शैब्य: (1) Koṭi-kāśya (son of Suratha) 3. 250. 4-5; 3. 251. 1, 4; (2) Govāsana 1. 90. 83; 6. 17. 20; 7. 70. 38; 7. 71. 11; (3) Vṛṣādarbhi (son of Śibi) 13. 94. 12 (8); (4) Auśīnara (son of Uśīnara = Śibi) 3. 120. 2. (cf. 1. 88. 6, 18); 7. 9. 65 (62); 12. 29. 38; 12. 281, 8 (?); (5) Grandson of Śaibya Auśī-nara (i. e. Śibi), not named 7. 9. 66; (6) Not identified 1. 1. 167 (= Auśīnara ?); 1. 1. 170; 3. 13. 27; (7) The following very probably refer to the same king (= Govā-sana, see above) fighting from the side of Pāṇḍavas 4. 67. 16; 5. 161. 6; 6. 23. 5; 6. 46. 54; 6. 47. 27; (8) The king on the side of Kauravas 6. 95. 27; (ii) शैब्या (f.): (1) Sunandā, wife of Pratīpa 1. 90. 46; (2) Wife of Kṛṣṇa, not named 16. 8. 71; (3) Wife of Dyumatsena, not named 3. 282. 2, 26; 3. 283. 10; (4) Wife of Sagara, not named 3. 104. 8 (6), 17; 3. 106. 10; (iii) Kāśipati, son of Śaibyā (?), not named, on the side of Kauravas: (शैब्यात्मजः काशिपतिः) 7. 7. 25.
शूकर: Śūkara m. (pl.): Name of a certain country (and its people). Their king, Kṛtin, gave as tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya many hun-dreds of excellent elephants (कृती तु राजा  … शूकराणां … । अददद् गजरत्नानां शतानि सुबहून्य् अपि ॥ ) 2. 48. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 52. 25: शूकराः देशभेदास् तेषाम्; however, see Edgerton's note on this stanza; {#“SUkara”#} epithet of elephants;  … cf. Kirfel, कोस्मोग्रफिए, p. 329, Cr. Edn. Vol. II, p. 507).
शूद्र: Śūdra m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya, first, among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5. (अपरन्ध्राश् च शूद्राश् च) 6. 10. 46; listed by him a second time among the northern Mleccha people (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … शूद्राभीराथ दरदाः) 6. 10. 63, 66; some Śūdras lived also in the west near the river Sarasvatī (शूद्रा-भीरगणाश् चैव ये चाश्रित्य सरस्वतीम्) 2. 29. 9 (see the Epic event No. 1 below). B. Their nature and way of living: They were harsh and were counted among Mleccha people (दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः) 6. 10. 64; (also cf. A. Location above and E. Future event below) they lived on fish, since they lived near the river Sarasvatī (वर्तयन्ति च मत्स्यैर् … ) 2. 29. 9. C. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedition to the west of Khā-ṇḍavaprastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10) brought them under control (शूद्रा-भीरगणाश् चैव … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 9-10; (2) On the eleventh day of war, Śūdras were among those who guarded at the extreme end (प्रपक्षाः) of the left side of the Śakaṭavyūha (7. 6. 15) of Kauravas (सव्यं पार्श्वम् अपालयन्) 7. 6. 4, 6. D. Past event: The river Sarasvatī for-merly disappeared at the Vinaśana tīrtha due to her hatred of Śūdras and Ābhīras (विनशनं नाम … शूद्राभीरान् प्रति द्वे-षाद् यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती) 9. 36. 1. E. Future event: Mārkaṇḍeya predicted that in the Kali age there would be many Mleccha kings among whom some would be Śūdras: these kings would be sinful, given to lies and ruling the wrong way (बहवो म्लेच्छराजानः पृथिव्यां … । मिथ्यानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः ॥  … शूद्रास् तथाभीरा … ) 3. 186. 29-30.
शूर: Śūra m. (pl): Name of a people. A. Location: Śūras lived probably in the north-west and were different from the Śūrasenas since they are mentioned along with Daradas, Bāhlīkas and others and since they are said to have brought tribute for the Rājasūya (see Epic event No. 1 below) and also because they are grouped with Yavanas (see B below). B. Special characteristic: According to a certain Brāhmaṇa reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the assembly of Kurus (8. 30. 7, 58), Śūras, like Yavanas, had the special characteristic of being clever in knowing everything (even though what was to be conveyed was not expressed in so many words) (सर्वज्ञा यवना राजञ् शूराश् चैव विशे-षतः) 8. 30. 80. C. Epic event: The Kṣatriyas among the Śūras, along with Vāyavyas and others, brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 12, 16; (Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, however, who like Śūrasenas, are sections of Yādavas, are reported to have not given tribute for the Rājasūya 2. 48. 42).
शूरसेन: Śūrasena m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; called Janapada at various places (4. 1. 9; 6. 18. 14; 6. 114. 77) and once Rāṣṭra (4. 1. 8). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शूरसेनाः कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 38; the country lay around the Kurus (परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 9; Pāṇḍavas while proceed-ing from Dvaitavana (3. 295. 2-3) to the country of Matsyas had to pass through Yakṛlloma and Śūrasena; their way lay to the north of Daśārṇa and south of Pāñcāla (उत्तरेण दशार्णांस् ते पाञ्चालान् दक्षिणेन तु ॥ अन्तरेण यकृल्लोमाञ् शूरसेनांश् च पाण्डवाः । … मत्स्यस्य विषयं प्राविशन् वनात्) 4. 5. 3-4; the city of Mathurā lay in it 2. 13. 44. B. Description: (a) of the country: delightful (रम्य), (रमणीय), rich in grain (बह्वन्न), and protected (गुप्त) 4. 1 8-9; (b) of the warriors: strong (बलवन्त्) and great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 112. 107, 111; valorous (विक्रान्त) 8. 4. 36; heroic, ready to give away their life (in war) (शूर, तनुत्यज्) 6. 18. 14; (शूर, वीर) 8. 32. 17. C. Characteristic: A certain Brāhmaṇa while reporting the characteristics of diffe-rent peoples to the Kuru assembly said that Śūrasenas were sacrifice incarnate (i. e. as sanctifying as sacrifice) (शूरसेनाश् च यज्ञः) 8. 30. 73. D. Epic events: (1) Śūrasenas, due to fear of Jarāsandha, resorted to the west (जरासन्धभयाद् एव प्रतीचीं दिशं आश्रिताः । शूरसेना … ) 2. 13. 24-25; (2) Having heard the news of the death of Haṃsa and Ḍibhaka, Jarā-sandha (left the country) of Śūrasenas to return to his town in Magadha (जरासन्-धः … स्वपुरं शूरसेनानां प्रययौ) 2. 13. 43; (See Edgerton's note on the stanza in Vol. II, p. 496: “This latter reading (°सेनेभ्यः) confirms my inter-pretation of शूरसेनानां as ablative genitive (Speyer, व्। स्। स्। § ७३) in the sense of “from the Śūrasena country””); (3) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south of Indraprastha (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; 2. 23. 9) first conquered the entire land of Śūrasenas (स शूरसेनान् कार्त्स्-न्येन पूर्वम् एवाजयत् प्रभुः) 2. 28. 2; (4) Arjuna mentioned Śūrasena among the countries in which Pāṇḍavas could stay during their अज्ञातवास 4. 1. 9; (5) Saṃ-jaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Śūrasenas no longer respected him and that they had joined the side of Yudhiṣṭhira recognizing his heroism (वीर्यज्ञास् तस्य धीमतः) 5. 53. 17; (6) Before the start of the war, Śūrasenas (who went to Kauravas) were among the twelve Janapadas who, led by Duḥśāsana and other sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, guarded the rear of Bhīṣma; they were all chariot-fighters twenty thou-sand strong (पृष्ठगोपास् तु भिष्मस्य  … रथा विंशतिसाहस्राः; महता रथ-वंशेन ते ऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम्) 6. 18. 10, 12, 14; (7) On the second day of the war, in the Mahāvyūha (6. 47. 10) of Kauravas Duryodhana asked Śūrasenas and others to protect Bhīṣma with their armies (भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु सह सैन्यपुरस्कृताः) 6. 47. 7, 9; Arjuna while proceeding to attack Bhīṣma killed many Śūrasenas in the Kaurava army 6. 48. 19; (8) On the third day, all Śūrasenas were posted at the ‘tail’ of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2-3) of Kauravas (पुच्छम् आसन् … शूरसेनाश् च सर्वशः) 6. 52. 7; (9) On the ninth day, Śūrasenas were among those who did not forsake Bhīṣma in the battle although they were being killed by sharp arrows (संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्य-मानाः शितैः शरैः) 6. 102. 7; (10) On the tenth day, incited by Duryodhana to attack Arjuna Śūrasenas marched on him; Arjuna burnt (ददाह) them with his divine weapons; when afflicted by arrows and when their chariots and banners were sha-ttered, their kings stopped attacking Arjuna (शरार्ता … विप्रकी र्णरथध्वजाः । नाभ्य-वर्तन्त राजानः सहिता वानरध्वजम्); Arjuna scattered their army (6. 112. 102-106, 109-112, 114-116); towards the end of that day, when the Kaurava army, afraid of Arjuna, fled from the battle, Śūrasenas were among those twelve Janapadas who, though afflicted by arrows and pained due to wounds, did not abandon Bhīṣma fighting with Arjuna (शूरसेनाः … द्वादशैते जन-पदा शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मं युध्यमानं किरीटिना ॥ ) 6. 114. 76-77; (11) On the eleventh day, Śūrasenas and others led by Duryodhana marched behind Karṇa in the Śakaṭavyūha (7. 6. 15) of Kauravas (तवात्मजं पुरस्-कृत्य सूतपुत्रस्य पृष्ठतः) 7. 6. 6-7; (12) On the twelfth day, Śūrasenas and others riding elephants, horses and chariots along with their foot-soldiers in hundreds and thousands stood at the ‘neck’ of the Suparṇavyūha of Kauravas (ग्रीवायां शूर-सेनाश् च … गजाश्वरथपत्त्यौघास् तस्थुः शतसहस्रशः) 7. 19. 8; (13) On the fourteenth day, ten thousand chariot-war-riors of Śūrasenas and others, led by Jaya and Kṛtavarman, tried to check the onward march of Arjuna towards Jayadratha 7. 66. 37; later, when Sudakṣiṇa and Śrutāyudha were killed, angered Śūrasenas and others, showered arrows on Arjuna; he killed six thousand of them; afraid, they fled, but returned and surrounded Arjuna; Arjuna cut off their arms and heads 7. 68. 2-5; towards the end of the day, while lamenting the death of Jayadratha, Duryodhana men-tioned Śūrasenas among those who fought for him but were killed by Arjuna (हता मदर्थं संग्रामे युध्यमानाः किरी-टिना) 7. 125. 31-32; (14) During the night war between the fourteenth and the fifteenth day, Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma killed Śūrasenas 7. 132. 24; 7. 136. 4; (15) On the seventeenth day, Kṛpa and others fought with Śūrasenas (on Pāṇḍavas' side); they fought a battle which led them to heaven in case of death (तेषाम् अन्तकरं  … स्वर्ग्यं यशस्करम्) 8. 32. 17-18; (16) At night, on the seventeenth day (निशि) while reporting the death of Karṇa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (8. 1. 25-26) Saṃjaya mentioned Śūrasenas among those who were killed in war 8. 4. 36. E. King Sunāman brother of Kaṃsa is referred to as king of Śūrasenas: शूरसेनराज् 7. 10. 8.
शृङ्गिन्: Śṛṅgin nara m. (pl.): Characterization of a people (not named). ‘Horned men’ mentioned along with Śakas, Tukhāras, Kaṅkas and Romaśas, who brought tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira in the form of an अर्बुद horses whose pedigree was noble and who went long distances; they also brought gold in crores totalling a पद्म; even then they were stopped at the gate (शकास् तुखाराः  … शृङ्गिणो नराः । महागमान् दूरगमान् गणितान् अर्बुदं हयान् ॥ कोटिशश् चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्मसंमितम् । बलिम् आदाय विविधं द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 47. 26-27.
शैवल: Śaivala m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शैवला बाह्लिकास् तथा) 6. 10. 52.
शौण्डिक: Śauṇḍika m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Epic event: Their chiefs (क्षत्रि-याः) brought tribute in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira; at the instance of the king, they were stopped at the gate by the gatekeepers and were asked to give more tribute; when each one of them further gave elephants (their description 2. 48. 19-20), they were allowed to enter (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशोऽजातशत्रवे । … तत्र स्म द्वारपालैस् ते प्रोच्यन्ते राजशासनात् । कृतकाराः सुबलयस् ततो द्वारम् अवाप्-स्यथ ॥ ) 2. 48. 15-16, 18-20 (Nī., Bom. Ed. 2. 52. 19: reads कृतकालाः and expla-ins the word as कृतप्रस्तावाः and remarks कृतद्वारा इति पाठे द्वारम् प्रतीहारेण सख्यम् । ). B. Their low social status: Originally Kṣatriyas, Śauṇḍikas were de-graded to the status of a वृषल due to their disregard of Brāhmaṇas (तास् ताः क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ ) 13. 33. 15. 17-19.
श्रेणि: Śreṇi m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) A. Description: Brought up in cow-herds (गोकुले नित्यसंवृद्धाः) and highly skilled in fighting (युद्धे परम-कोविदाः) 8. 4. 38. B. Epic event: At night of the seventeenth day (निशि 8. 1. 25), Saṃjaya, while reporting the death of Karṇa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, mentioned Śreṇis among those who were killed in thousands by Arjuna during the war (श्रेणयो बहुसाहस्राः संशप्तकगणाश् च ये । ते सर्वे पार्थम् आसाद्य गता वैवस्वतक्षयम् ॥ ) 8. 4. 38 (perhaps, the word श्रेणि does not refer to a people but means only ‘lines, rows of troops’ and refers to Gopālas who, though not directly mentioned are suggested by the expression (गोकुले नित्यसंवृद्धाः) and by their association with Saṃśaptakas, cf. Gopāla; see, however, the next entry).
श्रेणिमत्: Śreṇimant m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) Their glorious Kṣatriyas of noble birth, with weapons in hand, brought tribute in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (सुजातयः श्रेणिमन्तः श्रेयांसः शस्त्रपाणयः । आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे ॥ ) 2. 48. 16 (for other details of the tribute see Śau-ṇḍika above). (Is Śreṇimant name of a people or an adjective of Kṣatriyas mean-ing ‘Kṣatriyas in troops’ ? See Sreṇi above).
श्रेणिमन्त्: Śreṇimant m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) Their glorious Kṣatriyas of noble birth, with weapons in hand, brought tribute in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (सुजातयः श्रेणिमन्तः श्रेयांसः शस्त्रपाणयः । आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे ॥ ) 2. 48. 16 (for other details of the tribute see Śau-ṇḍika above). (Is Śreṇimant name of a people or an adjective of Kṣatriyas mean-ing ‘Kṣatriyas in troops’ ? See Sreṇi above).
